dwa_title: Review work orders or schedules to determine operations or procedures.
rationale: Work-order parsing and routing is well handled by MES/ERP rules and increasingly by document-reading models; the binding constraint is that the resulting operational decision is usually owned by a supervisor who reconciles the paperwork with shop-floor reality.

dwa_title: Evaluate reports or designs to determine work needs.
rationale: Reading a report or design and inferring what work is needed is squarely in LLM territory, but the inference drives resource commitments and rests on tacit context the documents omit.

dwa_title: Review details of technical drawings or specifications.
rationale: CAD/PDM software already extracts dimensions and tolerances automatically, but multimodal reading of legacy or annotated drawings remains error-prone and misread specifications propagate into costly physical rework.

dwa_title: Read documents to gather technical information.
rationale: This is pure information extraction from text — the core competence of retrieval-augmented language models; only verification of citation fidelity keeps a human nearby.

dwa_title: Review technical documents to plan work.
rationale: The reading half is highly exposed, but converting documents into an actual work plan requires site- and crew-specific context that is not in the documents.

dwa_title: Review blueprints or specifications to determine work requirements.
rationale: BIM-based quantity takeoff automates parts of this, yet interpreting blueprints against field conditions and code compliance still needs a licensed or experienced human whose misreading has structural consequences.

dwa_title: Collect evidence for legal proceedings.
rationale: Chain of custody and admissibility require a named, sworn human collector; digital-forensics tooling assists but cannot itself attest to provenance in court.

dwa_title: Examine crime scenes to obtain evidence.
rationale: Physical presence at an uncontrolled, one-time-only scene plus sworn accountability for evidence integrity makes this irreducibly embodied and human.

dwa_title: Examine records or other types of data to investigate criminal activities.
rationale: Transaction-monitoring and link-analysis systems already flag patterns at scale, but investigative conclusions that trigger legal action must be adopted and defended by an accountable investigator.

dwa_title: Investigate illegal or suspicious activities.
rationale: Investigation blends surveillance, interviewing and discretionary judgment about people's liberty; automated detection supplies leads but not the authority or the situational reading.

dwa_title: Obtain property information.
rationale: Title, assessor and MLS records are digitised and API-accessible, so retrieval and summarisation are routine; only physical inspection or unrecorded encumbrances require a person.

dwa_title: Retrieve information from electronic sources.
rationale: Querying databases and search systems is the canonical case of software doing the whole task; the only residual is judging source reliability.

dwa_title: Search files, databases or reference materials to obtain needed information.
rationale: Retrieval over indexed digital corpora is the canonical strength of search plus RAG systems; the only friction is non-digitised or access-restricted material.

dwa_title: Collect archival data.
rationale: Binding constraint is that much archival material is physical, uncatalogued or idiosyncratically stored, requiring on-site handling and provenance judgement before any machine reading can occur.

dwa_title: Gather organizational performance information.
rationale: Most performance data already flows through BI and ERP pipelines that automate collection; what resists is eliciting soft or undocumented performance signals from staff.

dwa_title: Gather physical survey data.
rationale: Data must be captured in situ; drones, LiDAR and GNSS rigs automate parts of the capture but instrument placement, ground truthing and access decisions still need a body on the terrain.

dwa_title: Collect data about project sites.
rationale: Site characterisation requires physical presence to observe conditions that remote sensing under-samples, such as subsurface, access and adjacent-use details.

dwa_title: Research hydrologic features or processes.
rationale: Literature synthesis and hydrologic model runs are highly machine-assisted, but field gauging and the framing of research questions and model assumptions remain expert-owned.

dwa_title: Research geological features or processes.
rationale: Geological interpretation depends on field sampling and outcrop observation plus contested inference from sparse evidence, limiting machines to data processing and image analysis.

dwa_title: Conduct climatological research.
rationale: The work is almost entirely computational over large archived datasets, so the constraint is not embodiment but the contested design of models and attribution claims that a scientist must defend.

dwa_title: Research industrial processes or operations.
rationale: Documentation and sensor-log analysis are strongly LLM-exposed, but understanding how a plant actually runs requires floor observation and interviews with operators.

dwa_title: Conduct scientific research of organizational behavior or processes.
rationale: Design, analysis and write-up are heavily machine-assisted, but human-subject data collection and research-ethics responsibility keep a named investigator in the loop.

dwa_title: Research impacts of environmental conservation initiatives.
rationale: Evaluating conservation outcomes hinges on contested counterfactual attribution and field monitoring; models can synthesise evidence but cannot settle the causal claim.

dwa_title: Investigate the environmental impact of projects.
rationale: Impact assessment is a regulated act whose findings must be certified by a qualified professional after site inspection and stakeholder consultation, regardless of how much analysis is automated.

dwa_title: Monitor environmental impacts of production or development activities.
rationale: Continuous sensing and telemetry automate the data capture, but interpreting anomalies against permit conditions and doing site verification still requires a qualified person on the ground.

dwa_title: Research environmental impact of industrial or development activities.
rationale: Literature synthesis and modelling are strongly LLM-exposed, but original impact research depends on field sampling and defensible methodological choices that a model cannot own.

dwa_title: Identify environmental concerns.
rationale: Screening for known concern categories is pattern-matching a model does well, but spotting unlisted or site-specific hazards requires contextual observation and professional responsibility for what was missed.

dwa_title: Evaluate environmental impact of operational or development activities.
rationale: Impact evaluations are contested professional judgments that regulators require a named, often licensed, assessor to stand behind, even though the analytic drafting is highly model-assistable.

dwa_title: Gather medical information from patient histories.
rationale: Abstracting structured and narrative data from existing records is close to pure text processing; the binding constraint is clinical accountability for omitted or misread findings.

dwa_title: Collect medical information from patients, family members, or other medical professionals.
rationale: Automated intake handles routine history-taking, but eliciting reluctant, distressed or inconsistent accounts from patients and families is a relational clinical skill with direct safety consequences.

dwa_title: Collect information from people through observation, interviews, or surveys.
rationale: Surveys are already fully instrumented, but direct observation requires presence and interviewing depends on rapport and adaptive probing that automated instruments handle shallowly.

dwa_title: Collect information about clients.
rationale: Digital intake forms and CRM enrichment already capture most structured client data; what remains is the conversational elicitation of context clients do not volunteer.

dwa_title: Research livestock management methods.
rationale: Synthesising published husbandry evidence is squarely in model territory, but validating methods against live herds and local conditions needs hands-on trial work.

dwa_title: Research crop management methods.
rationale: Agronomic literature and trial-data analysis are highly LLM-exposed; field plot experimentation and site-specific verification remain physical and seasonal.

dwa_title: Research sustainable agricultural processes or practices.
rationale: Sustainability research is information-synthesis heavy, but weighing contested trade-offs across yield, soil and emissions is a judgment call requiring empirical field validation.

dwa_title: Gather customer or product information to determine customer needs.
rationale: Behavioural analytics, product catalogues and conversational agents already infer customer needs end-to-end in commercial deployment; errors are cheap and instantly correctable.

dwa_title: Collect data about customer needs.
rationale: Automated surveys, review mining and conversational agents already harvest stated needs at scale; the binding constraint is eliciting unstated or latent needs through rapport-based interviewing, where a human interlocutor still gets richer signal.

dwa_title: Observe individuals' activities to gather information or compile evidence.
rationale: Fixed-camera analytics can log activity, but covert or mobile observation of a specific person in unstructured environments needs bodily presence, and evidentiary use requires a named observer who can testify to chain of custody.

dwa_title: Research genetic characteristics or expression.
rationale: Sequence and expression analysis is heavily computational and highly LLM/ML-exposed, but hypothesis framing plus wet-lab sample handling and assay execution remain hands-on outside a few automated screening facilities.

dwa_title: Research diseases or parasites.
rationale: Literature synthesis, epidemiological modelling and genomic analysis are strongly machine-assisted, but culturing pathogens, field sampling and biosafety-regulated experimentation anchor the work to physical labs and licensed investigators.

dwa_title: Conduct research of processes in natural or industrial ecosystems.
rationale: Sensor networks and remote sensing automate data capture, but designing the study, siting instruments and interpreting confounded ecosystem dynamics require in-situ presence and contestable expert inference.

dwa_title: Research microbiological or chemical processes or structures.
rationale: High-throughput robotic platforms and predictive models cover slices of the bench work, but end-to-end autonomous laboratories are rare in deployment; sample preparation and troubleshooting keep hands in the loop.

dwa_title: Classify organisms based on their characteristics or behavior.
rationale: Image classifiers, acoustic ID and DNA barcoding pipelines already assign taxa routinely and at scale; the residue is novel or cryptic taxa where formal taxonomic judgment and specimen handling still require a systematist.

dwa_title: Examine characteristics or behavior of living organisms.
rationale: Automated behaviour tracking works in instrumented enclosures, but examining organisms generally means handling and inspecting them in varied settings, which deployed systems cannot do.

dwa_title: Obtain written authorization to perform activities.
rationale: Permit and consent workflows are digitised and largely form-driven, but the authorisation must be sought and attested by a legally identifiable party, and negotiating with a reluctant grantor is relational.

dwa_title: Conduct anthropological or archaeological research.
rationale: Excavation and ethnographic fieldwork are irreducibly embodied and relational; only the literature review, artefact classification and write-up stages are meaningfully machine-assisted.

dwa_title: Conduct historical research.
rationale: The work is reading, collating and arguing over text, which models do well, but undigitised archives require physical access and source-credibility judgment plus hallucination risk keeps a historian accountable for the interpretation.

dwa_title: Conduct research on social issues.
rationale: Secondary data analysis and literature synthesis are highly exposed, but primary collection from human subjects involves consent, trust and ethics oversight, and causal claims about society remain contested expert judgment.

dwa_title: Conduct research to increase knowledge about medical issues.
rationale: Literature synthesis, hypothesis generation and data analysis are strongly model-exposed, but generating new medical knowledge still binds on wet-lab or clinical data collection and on a named principal investigator answerable for human-subject integrity.

dwa_title: Collect information about community health needs.
rationale: Secondary epidemiological and administrative data can be mined automatically, but the binding constraint is eliciting needs from residents and community organisations, which requires presence and trust-building.

dwa_title: Research engineering aspects of biological or chemical processes.
rationale: Models can review process literature, simulate kinetics and propose scale-up parameters, but validating bio/chemical process behaviour requires bench and pilot-plant experimentation that no deployed system runs autonomously.

dwa_title: Research methods to improve food products.
rationale: Formulation ideation and ingredient-literature search are highly model-exposed, but the decisive evidence comes from physical trials and sensory panels that need matter and human palates.

dwa_title: Research engineering applications of emerging technologies.
rationale: This is largely desk-based scanning and synthesis of technical literature and vendor data, which frontier models do well; what they cannot own is the engineer's discriminating judgement about which emerging technology is actually viable for a given context.

dwa_title: Research design or application of green technologies.
rationale: Green-technology assessment is document- and data-heavy and thus well within model reach, but site-specific feasibility and lifecycle assumptions remain contested calls a human must select and defend.

dwa_title: Conduct research to gain information about products or processes.
rationale: Written at high generality: the information-gathering core is retrieval and synthesis that tools already handle, while any empirical testing component pulls it back into the physical world.

dwa_title: Research advanced engineering designs or applications.
rationale: Advanced design research is analytic and simulation-driven, so models and solvers cover much of it; the constraint is novelty — frontier design questions have no precedent in training data and require verified experimental or computational validation.

dwa_title: Research energy production, use, or conservation.
rationale: Energy data are abundant and machine-readable, making modelling and literature review highly automatable; the sticking point is choosing scenario assumptions and reconciling field measurements with models.

dwa_title: Research human performance or health factors related to engineering or design activities.
rationale: Human-factors evidence is generated by observing and testing real people, so recruitment, instrumented trials and ethical oversight anchor it to humans even though the synthesis is model-exposed.

dwa_title: Research new technologies.
rationale: Technology scouting is almost pure reading and summarising over public information, the closest of this set to full automation; residual human value lies in filtering hype and relevance rather than in gathering.

dwa_title: Research product safety.
rationale: Standards review, hazard analysis and failure-data mining are model-tractable, but destructive and compliance testing is physical and product-liability regimes require a named, qualified person to stand behind the safety conclusion.

dwa_title: Examine debris to obtain information about causes of fires.
rationale: Fire cause determination requires hands-on sifting, sampling and spatial reading of a burn scene, and the conclusion is typically sworn to by a certified investigator in legal proceedings; only pattern-analysis support is machine-tractable.

dwa_title: Investigate system, equipment, or product failures.
rationale: Log analytics and diagnostic models can localize many failures, but root-cause work usually needs physical teardown and inspection plus a defensible causal judgment, so the machine contribution is hypothesis generation rather than closure.

dwa_title: Investigate safety of work environment.
rationale: Safety assessment binds on walking the site, observing actual worker behaviour and signing a regulated finding; sensors and checklist tools inform but cannot bear the statutory responsibility.

dwa_title: Interview employees, customers, or others to collect information.
rationale: Automated survey and chat interviews already harvest routine information, but eliciting candid or sensitive testimony depends on rapport, probing and reading the respondent, which conversational agents do poorly in adversarial or emotional settings.

dwa_title: Monitor video displays of medical equipment to ensure proper functioning.
rationale: Device self-diagnostics and central telemetry already flag malfunctions automatically, but alarm interpretation and the bedside response remain a licensed clinician's responsibility given the lethality of a missed fault.

dwa_title: Assess equipment functioning.
rationale: Condition-monitoring sensors and predictive-maintenance analytics cover much of the routine assessment, yet confirming a fault typically still requires physically handling or testing the machine.

dwa_title: Monitor industrial energy consumption or management.
rationale: Metering plus energy-management software performs continuous consumption tracking and anomaly detection end-to-end; humans mainly set targets and act on exceptions.

dwa_title: Monitor the productivity or efficiency of industrial operations.
rationale: MES and OEE dashboards already compute and report throughput and efficiency continuously from instrumented lines; the residual human role is interpreting causes and deciding interventions.

dwa_title: Monitor operational procedures in technical environments to ensure conformance to standards.
rationale: Digital procedure execution and audit trails automate conformance checking where work is logged, but observing whether people actually follow protocol in situ, and attesting to it, stays with a human.

dwa_title: Monitor the handling of hazardous materials or medical wastes.
rationale: Hazardous and medical waste handling is governed by regulations that name a responsible custodian and require physical verification of containment and manifests; tracking software supports but cannot substitute.

dwa_title: Monitor facilities or operational systems.
rationale: Building-management and SCADA platforms with alarming perform continuous facility surveillance today; humans are retained mostly for response and for unsensored conditions.

dwa_title: Monitor operational quality or safety.
rationale: Instrumented quality and safety metrics are readily machine-monitored, but the safety dimension carries a named-responsible-person requirement and depends on unmeasured, in-person cues; the activity as written is heterogeneous.

dwa_title: Monitor construction operations.
rationale: Construction sites are unstructured, changing physical environments where spotting unsafe or out-of-spec work requires being present and directing crews; drone and camera progress-capture automates documentation but not the supervisory judgment or safety liability.

dwa_title: Inspect operational processes.
rationale: Instrumented processes already self-monitor via SCADA and machine vision, but detecting the anomalies that no sensor covers still needs a person walking the line and interpreting context.

dwa_title: Monitor financial information.
rationale: Financial data is already digital and structured, so continuous tracking, variance flagging and narrative summarisation are routine software functions; only the sign-off on what the numbers mean stays human.

dwa_title: Monitor sales activities.
rationale: CRM and BI platforms already ingest pipeline data and generate alerts and forecasts end-to-end; the binding constraint is only whether anyone acts on the output.

dwa_title: Monitor patient progress or responses to treatments.
rationale: Models can synthesise labs, vitals and notes well, but clinical responsibility for interpreting a patient's trajectory and changing treatment is legally vested in a licensed clinician who must also observe the patient directly.

dwa_title: Monitor clients to evaluate treatment progress.
rationale: Judging whether a client is actually improving depends on rapport, affect and disclosure within a therapeutic relationship; the evidence is generated by the human contact itself.

dwa_title: Monitor patients following surgeries or other treatments.
rationale: Telemetry and early-warning scores automate detection, but post-procedure deterioration demands bedside assessment and immediate physical intervention under licensed accountability.

dwa_title: Monitor animal behavior or condition.
rationale: Precision-livestock sensors and vision systems reliably flag lameness, feeding and estrus in confined settings, yet diagnosing subtle condition changes and handling the animal still requires a stockperson on site.

dwa_title: Monitor health or behavior of people or animals.
rationale: Written broadly, this spans wearables-based tracking through direct custodial observation; the in-person duty of care over a living subject is what blocks end-to-end automation.

dwa_title: Monitor patient conditions during treatments, procedures, or activities.
rationale: Intraprocedural monitors already compute and alarm automatically, but standards of care and licensure require a named attendant physically present to interpret and respond within seconds.

dwa_title: Monitor nutrition related activities of individuals or groups.
rationale: Intake logging and nutrient analysis are well handled by software, but verifying what people actually eat and adjusting plans for medical or behavioural realities requires human observation and counselling.

dwa_title: Monitor performance of organizational members or partners.
rationale: Activity and output metrics are trivially instrumented, but appraising a person's performance carries employment-law and fairness consequences that a named supervisor must own, and much of the signal comes from relational context invisible to systems.

dwa_title: Monitor student performance.
rationale: Learning-management dashboards and automated grading already surface much of the signal, but interpreting a student's trajectory and deciding what it means for them remains a relational, accountable teacher act.

dwa_title: Monitor activities of individuals to ensure safety or compliance with rules.
rationale: Camera-based behaviour analytics can flag anomalies, but judging intent, intervening with the person and bearing responsibility for a safety call keeps a human present.

dwa_title: Patrol natural areas to ensure safety or enforce regulations.
rationale: Patrolling rough terrain and confronting visitors requires bodily presence and enforcement authority; drones and sensors supplement coverage but cannot issue citations or render aid.

dwa_title: Monitor work environment to ensure safety or adherence to specifications.
rationale: Fixed sensors and machine vision cover known hazard classes, but walking a site and noticing unanticipated deviations from spec still needs an on-site, answerable observer.

dwa_title: Patrol properties to maintain safety.
rationale: CCTV analytics and patrol robots are commercially deployed for surveillance, but physical presence, deterrence and hands-on response to incidents remain human.

dwa_title: Monitor alarm systems.
rationale: Alarm detection, verification and dispatch routing are already largely software; the residual human role is liability-driven confirmation of ambiguous or false alarms.

dwa_title: Monitor market conditions or trends.
rationale: Ingesting price, volume and news feeds and summarising trends is squarely a data-and-text task that deployed analytics plus LLMs already do continuously.

dwa_title: Monitor external affairs or events affecting business operations.
rationale: Scanning regulatory, political and competitive signals is text-native, but deciding which weak signals actually threaten the business relies on insider context and executive judgment.

dwa_title: Monitor environmental conditions to detect hazards.
rationale: Continuous gas, radiation and air-quality sensor networks automate detection well; the binding constraint is deploying and calibrating instruments in situ and owning the hazard call.

dwa_title: Measure environmental characteristics.
rationale: Instrumented and telemetered measurement is routine, but field sampling at unmonitored locations still requires someone to carry and operate the equipment.

dwa_title: Monitor activities affecting environmental quality.
rationale: Remote sensing and permit data flag likely violations, but linking observed activity to regulatory consequence requires site verification and a legally accountable officer.

dwa_title: Inspect condition of natural environments.
rationale: Satellite and drone imagery automate landscape-scale change detection, but assessing soil, species and habitat condition demands on-the-ground expert observation.

dwa_title: Monitor the security of digital information.
rationale: SIEM, EDR and anomaly-detection pipelines already automate detection and triage at scale, but adversarial novelty and the consequences of a missed or mishandled breach keep a named analyst in the escalation loop.

dwa_title: Monitor the performance of computer networks.
rationale: Network telemetry is machine-readable and thresholding/alerting is a solved, commercially standard function; humans are only pulled in for remediation decisions, not the monitoring itself.

dwa_title: Monitor computer system performance to ensure proper operation.
rationale: System observability stacks with automated alerting and self-healing runbooks already own continuous performance monitoring end-to-end in mainstream IT operations.

dwa_title: Determine operational compliance with regulations or standards.
rationale: Mapping evidence to regulatory text is squarely in reach of language models, but a compliance determination is a legally consequential act that an identified, often licensed, person must own.

dwa_title: Monitor medical facility activities to ensure adherence to standards or regulations.
rationale: Requires walking clinical areas, observing staff practice and interpreting accreditation standards under licensure; patient-safety accountability cannot be delegated to a system.

dwa_title: Inspect products or operations to ensure that standards are met.
rationale: Machine-vision and in-line gauging handle high-volume product inspection well, but heterogeneous items, tactile checks and operational context still require an inspector physically present.

dwa_title: Monitor operations to ensure compliance with safety or security policies or regulations.
rationale: Sensors and video analytics catch some violations, but safety and security oversight involves confronting behaviour in situ and carries statutory liability that attaches to a person.

dwa_title: Monitor organizational compliance with regulations.
rationale: Largely document- and data-based, so models can do much of the reading and cross-referencing, yet regulators require an accountable compliance officer to attest and to exercise interpretive discretion.

dwa_title: Verify that medical activities or operations meet standards.
rationale: Verification of clinical standards is an attestation act under professional licensure; the binding constraint is legal responsibility for patient harm, not analytic capability.

dwa_title: Monitor processes for compliance with standards.
rationale: Instrumented processes with statistical process control are already largely self-monitoring; the residual human role is interpreting drift and authorising deviations.

dwa_title: Monitor operational activities to ensure compliance with regulations or standard operating procedures.
rationale: Observing whether people actually follow SOPs in live operations demands presence and situational reading that logs and cameras only partially capture.

dwa_title: Evaluate construction projects to determine compliance with external standards or regulations.
rationale: Code compliance turns on physical inspection of partly concealed work at a site and on a certified inspector's signature that carries structural-safety liability.

dwa_title: Mark materials or objects for identification.
rationale: Labelling and marking is already mechanised in high-volume settings via print-and-apply and laser marking systems; the binding constraint is only the physical handling of varied, unstructured items in low-volume or field contexts.

dwa_title: Identify opportunities for green initiatives.
rationale: Scanning regulations, benchmarks and operational data to propose sustainability options is well within LLM reach, but selecting initiatives depends on organisational context and stakeholder buy-in that a model cannot own.

dwa_title: Identify potential customers.
rationale: Prospect identification and lead scoring are already productised in CRM and intent-data platforms; errors are cheap and self-correcting, so little human anchoring is needed.

dwa_title: Identify new applications for existing technologies.
rationale: Analogical search across technology and market literature is a strong LLM capability, but validating commercial viability requires tacit domain knowledge and contested strategic judgment.

dwa_title: Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency.
rationale: Process-mining and analytics tools plus LLM reasoning surface inefficiencies readily, but diagnosing real causes usually requires on-site observation and negotiation with the people doing the work.

dwa_title: Identify sustainable business practices.
rationale: Largely a research-and-synthesis task over standards, supply-chain data and best practice, which models do well; applicability to a specific operation and reporting credibility keep a human in charge.

dwa_title: Test patient heart or lung functioning.
rationale: Automated ECG and spirometry interpretation is mature, but attaching leads, coaching patient effort and validating results require a licensed clinician physically present.

dwa_title: Administer screening tests to determine abilities or treatment needs.
rationale: Digital screening instruments can be self-administered and auto-scored, yet eliciting valid responses from children, patients in distress or those with impairments is inherently relational and the resulting treatment decisions require a responsible professional.

dwa_title: Test patient hearing.
rationale: Automated audiometry and OAE screening exist and run largely unattended, but otoscopy, fitting transducers and handling unreliable responders require hands-on presence and licensed interpretation.

dwa_title: Test patient vision.
rationale: Autorefractors, automated visual field testing and retinal AI are commercially deployed, but positioning the patient and confirming refraction subjectively still anchors the task to a present, accountable examiner.

dwa_title: Conduct diagnostic tests to determine patient health.
rationale: Sample and image acquisition demand physical presence, and diagnostic conclusions carry licensure liability that requires a named clinician to sign regardless of model accuracy.

dwa_title: Test patient nervous system functioning.
rationale: Neurological examination and electrodiagnostic testing depend on skilled manual technique, patient cooperation and real-time adaptation; signal interpretation is assistable but the exam itself is not.

dwa_title: Test biological specimens to gather information about patient conditions.
rationale: High-throughput clinical analyzers already automate the assay chemistry, but specimen handling, pre-analytic prep and the licensed sign-off on abnormal or equivocal results keep a certified human in the loop.

dwa_title: Test green technologies or processes.
rationale: Testing novel or immature technologies requires designing bespoke physical trials and interpreting ambiguous performance data; only the analysis and reporting layer is readily machine-handled.

dwa_title: Test materials, solutions, or samples.
rationale: Automated sampling and instrumentation handle routine standardized assays well, but sample preparation, loading and non-standard matrices still demand hands in the lab.

dwa_title: Test products for functionality or quality.
rationale: Automated test rigs and machine-vision inspection are mature on high-volume production lines, but fixturing, low-volume or novel products, and functional edge cases still require a technician.

dwa_title: Analyze test results.
rationale: This is pure information processing over structured data, squarely in the sweet spot of statistical software and LLMs; the constraint is accountability for interpretation of anomalous or borderline results.

dwa_title: Test characteristics of materials or structures.
rationale: Universal testing machines and NDT equipment run instrumented protocols automatically, but specimen mounting and in-situ structural testing require physical presence.

dwa_title: Test fluids to identify contamination or other problems.
rationale: Inline sensors and automated fluid analyzers already do continuous contamination monitoring; the residual human role is drawing samples from equipment in the field.

dwa_title: Test quality of materials or finished products.
rationale: Automated QC stations and vision systems cover repetitive gauging and defect detection, but sampling plans, disposition of borderline lots and certification signatures remain human.

dwa_title: Inspect facilities or sites to determine if they meet specifications or standards.
rationale: Compliance inspection requires walking the site and a licensed inspector who is legally answerable for the certification, even where drones and checklists assist evidence gathering.

dwa_title: Inspect facilities for cleanliness.
rationale: Judging cleanliness means being physically present, looking under and behind things and sometimes swabbing; sensors and cameras cover only a fraction of the surfaces that matter.

dwa_title: Inspect condition or functioning of facilities or equipment.
rationale: Condition monitoring sensors and predictive analytics automate a growing share for instrumented assets, but most facility and equipment checks still need a technician on site with eyes and hands.

dwa_title: Inspect work sites to identify potential environmental or safety hazards.
rationale: Hazard identification is open-ended perception in an unstructured, changing site combined with statutory safety responsibility that must rest on a named competent person.

dwa_title: Inspect work environments to ensure safety.
rationale: Safety walkthroughs require being bodily present to notice open-ended, unanticipated hazards and to engage workers; the binding constraint is that a certified inspector's signature carries legal liability for what was missed.

dwa_title: Inspect areas for compliance with sanitation standards.
rationale: Sanitation inspection depends on in-situ sensory checks (surfaces, temperatures, odours, pest signs) in cluttered, variable premises; enforcement authority and citation liability rest with a named official.

dwa_title: Verify alignment of structures or equipment.
rationale: Laser trackers, total stations and vision metrology already measure alignment automatically, but mounting targets, accessing the structure and interpreting out-of-tolerance causes still need a technician on site.

dwa_title: Inspect finished products to locate flaws.
rationale: Machine-vision and anomaly-detection inspection is mature and running unattended on production lines; the residual constraint is handling/presentation of parts and rare defect classes outside the training distribution.

dwa_title: Inspect equipment or systems.
rationale: Instrumented condition monitoring covers sensored assets, but generic inspection still means physically reaching, opening and sensing equipment that is not wired for telemetry.

dwa_title: Inspect equipment to ensure safety or proper functioning.
rationale: Safety-critical clearance to operate typically requires a competent person to attest in person; sensors can flag faults but cannot assume the liability for declaring equipment safe.

dwa_title: Inspect equipment to ensure proper functioning.
rationale: Built-in self-test and predictive-maintenance analytics automate the checks on modern connected equipment, but most legacy plant still needs a human to look, listen and actuate controls.

dwa_title: Inspect safety equipment to ensure proper functioning.
rationale: Extinguishers, harnesses, alarms and eyewash stations are dispersed physical items whose inspection is codified as a tagged, signed, legally mandated act by a qualified person.

dwa_title: Examine medical instruments or equipment to ensure proper operation.
rationale: Devices increasingly self-diagnose, but patient-safety regulation requires a biomedical technician or clinician to physically verify and document fitness for use before a device touches a patient.

dwa_title: Conduct validation tests of equipment or processes.
rationale: Automated test rigs and scripted protocols execute the runs and models can draft protocols and reports, but in regulated validation (IQ/OQ/PQ, GxP) a named human must approve the acceptance decision.

dwa_title: Test computer hardware performance.
rationale: Benchmark suites, burn-in rigs and diagnostic firmware already run and report unattended; humans are needed mainly to rack the hardware and attach instrumentation.

dwa_title: Test computer system operations to ensure proper functioning.
rationale: Continuous monitoring, synthetic transactions and automated regression/test pipelines are standard practice; the remaining human role is triaging ambiguous failures and owning production go/no-go calls.

dwa_title: Test software performance.
rationale: Load, profiling and regression testing are already scripted into CI/CD pipelines and the interpretation of results is text-and-metric reasoning that models handle well; the binding constraint is only deciding which performance targets matter.

dwa_title: Check physical condition of people or animals.
rationale: Palpation, auscultation and handling of a living, possibly uncooperative body cannot be done from a terminal, and a licensed examiner must own the finding.

dwa_title: Examine patients to assess general physical condition.
rationale: The physical examination requires hands-on presence and clinical licensure; models can structure and interpret findings but cannot elicit them or bear the medico-legal responsibility.

dwa_title: Examine mouth, teeth, gums, or related facial structures.
rationale: Intraoral inspection demands instruments in a patient's mouth; AI caries detection on radiographs assists but the examination and its diagnostic sign-off remain a licensed clinician's act.

dwa_title: Measure the physical or physiological attributes of patients.
rationale: Automated vitals monitors, kiosks and wearables already capture most physiological measures without a clinician; the residual constraint is positioning the patient and applying sensors correctly.

dwa_title: Evaluate characteristics of archival or historical objects.
rationale: Provenance, authenticity and condition assessment rests on tacit connoisseurship plus hands-on material inspection; models can supply comparative research but not the physical appraisal.

dwa_title: Examine condition of property or products.
rationale: Machine vision handles repeatable product defect inspection on a line, but examining varied property in situ still needs someone walking the site and lifting covers.

dwa_title: Test facilities for environmental hazards.
rationale: Fixed sensors automate continuous monitoring, but hazard surveys require sampling in specific physical locations and certified inspectors whose names go on the report.

dwa_title: Test performance of electrical, electronic, mechanical, or integrated systems or equipment.
rationale: Built-in self-test, automated test equipment and telemetry diagnostics cover much of the measurement, yet hooking up probes and fixturing non-instrumented hardware still requires hands.

dwa_title: Test mechanical systems to ensure proper functioning.
rationale: Condition-monitoring sensors flag anomalies automatically, but functional run-up checks of mechanical assemblies typically require an operator present to actuate and observe them.

dwa_title: Measure ingredients or substances to be used in production processes.
rationale: Gravimetric batching and automated dosing systems are mature, commercially standard equipment; the task is a deterministic measurement against a recipe.

dwa_title: Measure the level or depth of water or other liquids.
rationale: Ultrasonic, float and pressure level sensors with telemetry already replace manual gauging almost everywhere; only initial installation needs a physical presence.

dwa_title: Measure physical or chemical properties of materials or objects.
rationale: Instrumentation and automated analysers handle the measurement itself, but sample preparation, fixturing and instrument calibration still require hands on the material; the binding constraint is physical sample handling rather than cognition.

dwa_title: Measure radiation levels.
rationale: Fixed area monitors, dosimeter networks and drone-mounted detectors already log radiation continuously without humans, but contamination surveys of specific surfaces and the regulatory sign-off on exposure findings keep a licensed person in the loop.

dwa_title: Measure distances or dimensions.
rationale: Coordinate measuring machines, laser scanners, LiDAR and machine vision are commercially routine for dimensional metrology; the residual human role is placing or presenting the object, not determining the number.

dwa_title: Calculate weights, volumes or other characteristics of materials.
rationale: This is deterministic arithmetic over densities, geometry and material tables, already embedded in CAD and process-control software; nothing physical or contested binds it.

dwa_title: Measure ingredients.
rationale: Industrial batching and gravimetric dosing systems are fully automated, but the same activity in kitchens, pharmacies and small-batch shops requires manual handling of variable containers and materials that no deployed manipulator handles economically.

dwa_title: Estimate time or monetary resources needed to complete projects.
rationale: Models can assemble takeoffs, historical analogues and schedules quickly, but the binding constraint is contested assumptions about scope, productivity and risk that a named estimator must own when the bid is committed.

dwa_title: Estimate operational costs.
rationale: Operational cost modelling runs on structured historical data that software already aggregates well; what resists is the forward-looking assumption setting about utilisation, inflation and vendor behaviour.

dwa_title: Estimate green project costs.
rationale: Green retrofit and energy project costing depends on thin, fast-moving data on incentives, technology pricing and site-specific conditions, so model output must be re-based by a human with current market knowledge.

dwa_title: Estimate costs for projects or productions.
rationale: Digital takeoff and parametric estimating tools automate the quantity and unit-rate mechanics, but scope interpretation from incomplete drawings or scripts, and ownership of the committed number, stay human.

dwa_title: Survey land or properties.
rationale: GNSS, robotic total stations and drone photogrammetry capture the data with little manual effort, but boundary determination requires on-site evidence interpretation and a licensed surveyor's seal that statute assigns to a named individual.

dwa_title: Calculate geographic positions from survey data.
rationale: Coordinate reduction, datum transformation and least-squares network adjustment are solved algorithms running inside standard survey software; only blunder adjudication and certification need a person.

dwa_title: Survey land or bodies of water to measure or determine features.
rationale: Autonomous survey vessels, multibeam sonar and UAV LiDAR automate data capture on open terrain and water, but mobilising equipment, handling access, weather and obstructed sites still demands a crew in place.

dwa_title: Assess locations for potential green technology installations.
rationale: Solar/wind siting analytics from GIS, LIDAR and irradiance data are commercially strong, but final suitability requires on-site structural, shading and interconnection verification signed by an engineer.

dwa_title: Assess patient work, living, or social environments.
rationale: Home and workplace assessment requires physical presence and clinical rapport to observe hazards and social context that patients under-report; a licensed clinician owns the resulting care plan.

dwa_title: Evaluate program effectiveness.
rationale: Data synthesis, indicator construction and report drafting are highly model-exposed, but attributing outcomes to a program and defending that causal claim to stakeholders remains a contested human judgment.

dwa_title: Evaluate the effectiveness of counseling or educational programs.
rationale: Outcome data and survey text can be analysed automatically, but judging counseling efficacy hinges on interpreting participant experience and clinical context that requires human observation.

dwa_title: Evaluate effectiveness of personnel policies or practices.
rationale: HR analytics platforms already surface policy impacts on turnover and equity, but legal exposure and employee-relations nuance keep an accountable HR professional in the loop.

dwa_title: Evaluate effectiveness of educational programs.
rationale: Assessment data mining is mature, but curricular judgment, classroom observation and accreditation defensibility require an educator's sign-off.

dwa_title: Evaluate civic projects or public policies.
rationale: Policy evaluation is heavily text-and-data based and thus model-exposed, but it involves contested value tradeoffs and political legitimacy that demand a named human evaluator.

dwa_title: Assess educational needs of students.
rationale: Adaptive diagnostics identify skill gaps well, but distinguishing disability, motivation, language and home-context causes requires relational observation and carries placement liability.

dwa_title: Administer tests to assess educational needs or progress.
rationale: Computer-based test delivery and scoring are routine, but proctoring, accommodations and standardized-administration protocols still require a responsible human present.

dwa_title: Prepare tests.
rationale: Item generation aligned to standards is a core LLM strength; the remaining constraint is validity review and psychometric vetting of high-stakes items.

dwa_title: Evaluate student work.
rationale: Automated essay and code scoring is deployed and accurate on average, but grades are consequential records that an instructor must own, and formative feedback depends on knowing the student.

dwa_title: Evaluate performance of educational staff.
rationale: Teacher evaluation drives employment decisions subject to union contracts and due process, requiring classroom observation and a named supervisor's accountable judgment.

dwa_title: Evaluate employee performance.
rationale: Models can aggregate metrics and draft appraisal narratives, but employment law, fairness challenges and the supervisory relationship require a named manager to own the rating.

dwa_title: Evaluate capabilities or training needs.
rationale: Skills-gap inference from assessments and role profiles is well suited to models; the binding constraint is tacit knowledge of the individual and the organisation's priorities that only surfaces in conversation.

dwa_title: Evaluate performance of applicants, trainees, or employees.
rationale: Automated scoring of applicants and trainees exists but is legally constrained by anti-discrimination and adverse-impact rules that demand a human decision-maker of record.

dwa_title: Evaluate quality of materials or products.
rationale: Machine-vision and sensor-based inspection is already routine on production lines; what remains human is sampling odd cases, tactile or sensory checks, and disposition of borderline defects.

dwa_title: Assess physical conditions of patients to aid in diagnosis or treatment.
rationale: Physical examination requires hands on the patient plus a licensed clinician answerable for the diagnostic conclusion; devices can capture signals but not perform the assessment.

dwa_title: Evaluate patient functioning, capabilities, or health.
rationale: Functional assessment blends observed physical performance with patient report and clinical licensure accountability, none of which a system can own end-to-end.

dwa_title: Evaluate patient outcomes to determine effectiveness of treatments.
rationale: Outcome tracking over structured records is highly amenable to model analysis, but attributing improvement to a treatment and acting on it is a licensed clinical judgment.

dwa_title: Evaluate treatment options to guide medical decisions.
rationale: Weighing therapeutic options is almost pure information reasoning that models do well, yet medical licensure and liability require a named prescriber to decide.

dwa_title: Assess skin or hair conditions.
rationale: Image-based dermatological and trichological classifiers are commercially deployed and accurate on common presentations, but palpation, lighting control and triage responsibility keep a person in the loop.

dwa_title: Assess the cost effectiveness of products, projects, or services.
rationale: Cost-benefit modelling is quantitative and tool-supported, so models do the analysis readily; the constraint is choosing assumptions and defending them to decision-makers.

dwa_title: Evaluate new technologies or methods.
rationale: Literature synthesis and comparative appraisal are core model strengths, but credible evaluation usually requires hands-on trialling and contextual fit judgment.

dwa_title: Evaluate potential of products, technologies, or resources.
rationale: Forecasting potential rests on contested assumptions about future markets and capabilities where evidence is thin, so models can scaffold the case but cannot settle it.

dwa_title: Evaluate the characteristics of green technologies.
rationale: Most of the work is synthesising specifications, lifecycle data and standards, which a model does well, but credible assessment still depends on field/test data and contested sustainability criteria that a human must select and defend.

dwa_title: Assess product or process usefulness.
rationale: Usefulness is defined relative to user needs and organisational goals that are elicited from people and weighed subjectively; models can structure and argue the case but cannot own the value judgement.

dwa_title: Assess database performance.
rationale: Query telemetry, APM dashboards and automatic index/plan advisors already measure and diagnose database performance end-to-end; the binding constraint is acting on findings in production, not detecting them.

dwa_title: Evaluate characteristics of equipment or systems.
rationale: Instrumented systems can be evaluated from sensor data, but many equipment characteristics only reveal themselves through hands-on inspection and physical test setups at the machine.

dwa_title: Evaluate utility of software or hardware technologies.
rationale: Comparing specs, benchmarks and fit-to-requirement is nearly pure information work well within model reach; what blocks full automation is procurement accountability and tacit knowledge of the local environment.

dwa_title: Evaluate characteristics of products.
rationale: Machine vision and automated test rigs already grade many product attributes, but attributes like feel, taste, durability or fit still require a person handling the item.

dwa_title: Evaluate scholarly materials.
rationale: Reading and critiquing scholarly text is squarely in an LLM's wheelhouse, but originality and significance judgements are contested and scholarly norms require a named, reputationally accountable reviewer.

dwa_title: Evaluate project designs to determine adequacy or feasibility.
rationale: Design adequacy reviews can be heavily assisted by code-checking and simulation, but licensure and liability regimes require a qualified human to attest that the design is sound.

dwa_title: Analyze data to determine project feasibility.
rationale: The modelling and sensitivity analysis are automatable, but the assumptions driving a feasibility verdict are contestable and carry investment consequences someone must stand behind.

dwa_title: Verify accuracy of records.
rationale: Rule-based reconciliation, validation logic and OCR-plus-matching already handle routine record verification; humans are retained mainly for exception handling and attestation.

dwa_title: Verify mathematical calculations.
rationale: Recomputation and cross-footing are deterministic and have been machine-performed for decades; the only residual need is identifying which figures matter and signing off.

dwa_title: Check quality of diagnostic images.
rationale: Automated artifact and exposure QC software is deployed, but deciding a study is non-diagnostic and repeating it requires the patient present and a clinically accountable operator.

dwa_title: Verify information or specifications.
rationale: Cross-checking stated values against authoritative sources is highly rule-based and well served by validation software and LLM extraction, but the binding constraint is access to trustworthy reference sources and the residual need for a human to sign off on discrepancies.

dwa_title: Verify customer credit information.
rationale: Credit bureau APIs and automated decisioning engines already perform this end-to-end at scale; remaining human involvement is mostly exception handling and regulatory adverse-action justification.

dwa_title: Evaluate data quality.
rationale: Profiling, anomaly detection and rule-based data-quality tooling are mature, but deciding whether observed quality is fit for a given purpose remains a contextual professional judgment.

dwa_title: Verify accuracy of data.
rationale: Automated reconciliation, checksum and validation-rule systems handle most accuracy checking already; the limit is verifying against ground truth that exists only outside the system.

dwa_title: Check data for recording errors.
rationale: Detecting transcription and recording errors is a pattern-matching task that validation rules, double-entry checks and models perform reliably and cheaply.

dwa_title: Compile operational data.
rationale: Operational data aggregation is the core use case of ETL pipelines and BI reporting; the remaining friction is integrating unstructured or manually captured sources.

dwa_title: Compile technical information or documentation.
rationale: LLMs excel at gathering, structuring and drafting technical documentation, but sourcing authoritative specifications from engineers and certifying correctness keeps a human owner.

dwa_title: Compile data or documentation.
rationale: Generic collection and collation of documents and data is largely a retrieval-and-formatting task already handled by document management and LLM tooling.

dwa_title: Compile specialized bibliographies or lists of materials.
rationale: Catalogue search, citation management and LLM synthesis cover bibliography compilation well; the binding issue is relevance curation for a specific patron's need and source-verification against hallucination.

dwa_title: Compile environmental or climatological data.
rationale: Environmental and climate data flows are already collected by automated sensor networks and ingested into standard archives; human effort persists mainly in instrument maintenance and QC of legacy records.

dwa_title: Compile geographic or related data.
rationale: Remote sensing, GPS feeds and automated GIS ingestion dominate geographic data compilation; field survey and ground-truthing remain the embodied residual.

dwa_title: Verify accuracy of patient information.
rationale: Automated eligibility checks and record matching help, but confirming identity, demographics and history usually requires interrogating the patient directly and a clinician or registrar is accountable for a misidentification with potentially serious clinical consequences.

dwa_title: Examine documents to verify adherence to requirements.
rationale: Document intake and rule-checking are well served by OCR plus LLM extraction, but requirement sets are idiosyncratic and edge-case calls still route to a named reviewer who accepts or rejects.

dwa_title: Review documents or materials for compliance with policies or regulations.
rationale: Regulatory interpretation is textual and highly LLM-exposed, but ambiguity in how rules apply to a specific document plus the liability attached to a compliance determination keeps a human as the decision owner.

dwa_title: Review environmental permits, plans, or reports.
rationale: Permit and report review is document-based and highly assistable, but the determination is a regulatory act that typically requires a licensed or delegated official to sign and defend.

dwa_title: Proofread documents, records, or other files to ensure accuracy.
rationale: Grammar, consistency and data-accuracy checking against source records is exactly what deployed text tools already do end-to-end; residual human involvement is stylistic preference, not capability.

dwa_title: Review plans or proposals for environmental conservation.
rationale: Conservation plan review weighs contested ecological trade-offs and stakeholder interests against incomplete field data, so models can summarise and flag but cannot settle the scientific judgment call.

dwa_title: Assess compliance with environmental laws.
rationale: Compliance assessment typically rests on site observation, sampling and interviews, and the finding carries enforcement consequences that statute assigns to an authorised inspector.

dwa_title: Evaluate green operations or programs for compliance with standards or regulations.
rationale: Standards conformance for programs is largely evidence-document review that models handle well, but verification of what actually happens operationally requires on-site corroboration and a certifiable human conclusion.

dwa_title: Evaluate plans or specifications to determine technological or environmental implications.
rationale: Reasoning from specifications to downstream technical and environmental consequences is analytic and model-assistable, but it is forecasting under genuine scientific uncertainty where expert engineers legitimately disagree.

dwa_title: Conduct financial or regulatory audits.
rationale: Analytics already automate sampling, reconciliation and anomaly detection, yet audit opinions are statutorily signed by a licensed individual who bears personal and firm liability for the conclusion.

dwa_title: Review customer insurance information.
rationale: Coverage and eligibility verification runs against structured policy databases with established clearinghouse automation; exceptions and customer explanation are the shrinking human remainder.

dwa_title: Protect patients or staff members using safety equipment.
rationale: Donning, positioning and applying protective equipment on real bodies in a clinical room is irreducibly physical and carries direct patient-safety liability.

dwa_title: Follow protocols or regulations for healthcare activities.
rationale: Following clinical protocol is an act of bedside execution under professional licensure; systems can prompt and check adherence but a credentialed clinician must perform and answer for it.

dwa_title: Locate natural resources using geospatial or other environmental data.
rationale: ML prospectivity mapping over remote-sensing and geophysical stacks is deployed and genuinely productive, but the binding constraint is sparse, noisy ground truth: committing capital to a drill target rests on expert geological inference that models cannot yet own.

dwa_title: Determine geographic coordinates.
rationale: GNSS receivers, RTK networks and georeferencing software compute coordinates deterministically; the only residual human element is physically occupying the point and certifying the result where survey law requires a licensed signature.

dwa_title: Analyze geological samples.
rationale: Instrumental assay (XRF, XRD, automated mineralogy) is automated, but sample preparation, thin-section handling and petrographic description require hands on rock, which anchors the activity physically even though the interpretive write-up is model-exposed.

dwa_title: Analyze environmental data.
rationale: The statistical pipeline from sensor or monitoring data to trend detection is highly automatable, but regulatory environmental conclusions must be defensible and signed by a qualified professional, keeping a human in the loop on interpretation.

dwa_title: Analyze geological or geographical data.
rationale: Subsurface and spatial datasets are ambiguous and underdetermined, so models accelerate processing and hypothesis generation while the binding constraint remains expert reconciliation of conflicting geological interpretations.

dwa_title: Analyze Geographic Information Systems (GIS) data for use in green applications.
rationale: Standard GIS overlay, suitability and siting analyses are scriptable and increasingly agent-driven; what resists is choosing weighting criteria and defending siting tradeoffs to stakeholders.

dwa_title: Analyze physical, survey, or geographic data.
rationale: Survey adjustment and spatial data reduction are already software-driven, but blunder detection and legally certified boundary or engineering conclusions still attach to a licensed human.

dwa_title: Estimate demand for products or services.
rationale: Automated demand-forecasting engines run unattended in retail and supply chain, yet structural breaks, promotions and new products require human override because the historical series stops being informative.

dwa_title: Forecast economic, political, or social trends.
rationale: Models can synthesise vast evidence and articulate scenarios, but the activity is irreducibly contested prediction where accuracy is unverifiable in advance and institutions want a named forecaster to defend the call.

dwa_title: Analyze market conditions or trends.
rationale: Gathering, summarising and comparing market evidence is squarely in frontier-model territory; the constraint is proprietary or tacit channel knowledge and the strategic weighting of ambiguous signals.

dwa_title: Analyze website or related online data to track trends or usage.
rationale: Web analytics platforms already collect, segment, anomaly-detect and narrate usage trends automatically, and errors are cheap and reversible, so nothing binds a human to the loop.

dwa_title: Analyze market or customer related data.
rationale: Segmentation, churn scoring and cohort analysis over CRM data are commodity automated pipelines; residual human input is framing the business question and privacy compliance rather than the analysis itself.

dwa_title: Analyze market research data.
rationale: Survey coding, segmentation and cross-tab analysis are already substantially tool-driven and LLM-tractable; the binding constraint is framing which commercial question the data actually answers and defending the inference to decision-makers.

dwa_title: Analyze risks to minimize losses or damages.
rationale: Quantitative loss modelling is automatable but tail risks and novel exposures are precisely where models fail; an accountable human underwriter, actuary or risk officer must own the residual judgment.

dwa_title: Apply mathematical principles or statistical approaches to solve problems in scientific or applied fields.
rationale: Symbolic and statistical computation is machine-native, but selecting an appropriate model and validating that its assumptions hold for the physical or applied problem still requires expert framing.

dwa_title: Analyze data to identify trends or relationships among variables.
rationale: Trend detection and correlation discovery are routinely performed end-to-end by deployed analytics and AutoML pipelines; the human residue is distinguishing spurious from meaningful relationships.

dwa_title: Evaluate technical data to determine effect on designs or plans.
rationale: Propagating a technical finding through a design requires integrating tacit constraints and code obligations, and in licensed engineering contexts a named professional must sign off on the design change.

dwa_title: Analyze design requirements for computer or electronics systems.
rationale: Requirements are textual and highly LLM-tractable, but they arrive incomplete and contradictory from stakeholders, so eliciting and reconciling intent remains the bottleneck.

dwa_title: Evaluate designs or specifications to ensure quality.
rationale: Rule-based design-rule and specification checking is automated in CAD/EDA toolchains, but quality sign-off is a formal accountability act tied to a responsible reviewer.

dwa_title: Analyze green technology design requirements.
rationale: Standards, incentives and lifecycle data are documentary and machine-readable, but green criteria are contested and rapidly shifting, so defensible interpretation still rests with a human specialist.

dwa_title: Analyze project data to determine specifications or requirements.
rationale: Deriving specifications from project data is a synthesis task models handle well on clean inputs; the constraint is that much of the governing context is unwritten and must be negotiated with clients and teams.

dwa_title: Analyze design or requirements information for mechanical equipment or systems.
rationale: Mechanical analysis depends on geometry, materials behaviour and failure modes that simulation tools assist with but cannot certify; licensed engineering responsibility anchors the final determination.

dwa_title: Evaluate environmental or sustainability projects.
rationale: Evaluation typically requires site verification, stakeholder consultation and weighing contested ecological and social values, none of which a model can discharge or be held answerable for.

dwa_title: Analyze costs and benefits of proposed designs or projects.
rationale: The arithmetic of cost-benefit analysis is trivially automatable, but the results hinge on assumptions, discount rates and scope choices that are contestable and must be owned by a human analyst.

dwa_title: Analyze health-related data.
rationale: Health data analysis is largely information processing that models and analytics tools handle well, but clinical and regulatory governance requires a licensed human to own conclusions drawn from patient data.

dwa_title: Analyze patient data to determine patient needs or treatment goals.
rationale: Setting treatment goals is a licensed clinical act tied to patient preferences and consent; models can draft the assessment but scope-of-practice rules bind responsibility to a clinician.

dwa_title: Analyze test data or images to inform diagnosis or treatment.
rationale: FDA-cleared imaging and lab-interpretation AI is deployed but almost universally as a flagging or triage aid; a radiologist or pathologist must sign the diagnostic report.

dwa_title: Analyze medical data to determine cause of death.
rationale: Cause-of-death determination is a statutory certification by a named medical examiner or coroner with legal consequences, and often depends on physical examination evidence.

dwa_title: Calculate numerical data for medical activities.
rationale: Dose and formula calculations are deterministic and already embedded in calculators and pharmacy systems; the residual constraint is mandated independent human verification because arithmetic errors can be lethal.

dwa_title: Analyze quantitative data to determine effectiveness of treatments or therapies.
rationale: Statistical evaluation of treatment effectiveness is highly codified and tool-supported, but confounding, endpoint selection and regulatory sign-off keep a qualified analyst accountable.

dwa_title: Analyze data to inform operational decisions or activities.
rationale: BI and analytics pipelines plus LLM interpretation cover most of the analytic core; the binding constraint is that the decision context and consequences sit with an accountable manager.

dwa_title: Analyze data to identify or resolve operational problems.
rationale: Anomaly detection and root-cause suggestion are well automated, but confirming causes and enacting fixes usually requires tacit process knowledge and access to the physical or organisational system.

dwa_title: Analyze traffic data.
rationale: Traffic counting, flow modelling and signal-timing optimisation run on deployed sensor and simulation platforms with minimal human input; engineering sign-off applies mainly when designs change infrastructure.

dwa_title: Analyze energy usage data.
rationale: Metering, building-management analytics and automated disaggregation already produce energy usage findings end-to-end; humans mainly choose which recommended retrofits to fund.

dwa_title: Analyze operational or research data.
rationale: Generic data analysis is squarely in the wheelhouse of code-writing models and statistical tooling; framing the question and validating that results mean something remain human-owned.

dwa_title: Analyze operational data to evaluate operations, processes or products.
rationale: Performance evaluation against metrics is routinely dashboarded and can be narrated by models, but judging whether a process or product is acceptable involves contested standards and organisational stakes.

dwa_title: Evaluate energy production data.
rationale: Energy output data is already streamed into SCADA and analytics platforms that flag anomalies and compute performance metrics automatically; what remains human is deciding which deviations matter operationally and committing to a response.

dwa_title: Interpret research or operational data.
rationale: Interpretation is pure symbolic reasoning over structured data, which frontier models handle well, but grounding conclusions in undocumented process context and owning the inference still requires the domain expert.

dwa_title: Model operational processes.
rationale: Code generation and simulation tooling can build and calibrate process models quickly, but choosing the abstraction, boundary conditions and validation criteria is a contested modelling judgment that no deployed system owns.

dwa_title: Appraise environmental impact of regulations or policies.
rationale: The evidence base is documentary and highly amenable to model synthesis, but environmental impact appraisal rests on contested causal and valuation assumptions that expert reviewers and statutory processes must adjudicate.

dwa_title: Analyze environmental regulations to ensure organizational compliance.
rationale: Mapping regulatory text onto operational facts is exactly what language models do well, yet compliance determinations carry legal liability that requires a named accountable officer to certify.

dwa_title: Analyze impact of legal or regulatory changes.
rationale: Tracking and summarising legal change is largely text analysis, but forecasting how a change will bite on a specific organisation involves ambiguity and enforcement-practice knowledge that models get wrong in ways only counsel can catch.

dwa_title: Evaluate applicable laws and regulations to determine impact on organizational activities.
rationale: The binding constraint is professional responsibility: legal applicability opinions must be attributable to a licensed or officer-level human even when the analytic draft is machine-produced.

dwa_title: Analyze laboratory specimens to detect abnormalities or other problems.
rationale: High-throughput analysers and image-based screening already automate much of the detection step, but specimen handling plus regulated result verification and sign-off keep a certified technologist or pathologist in the loop.

dwa_title: Analyze forensic evidence to solve crimes.
rationale: Instruments and database matching automate parts of the workflow, but chain-of-custody, admissibility and courtroom testimony legally require an identifiable expert to own every interpretive step.

dwa_title: Analyze crime scene evidence.
rationale: Evidence must be recognised, collected and documented in situ under adversarial legal scrutiny; neither the embodiment nor the sworn accountability can be delegated to a system.

dwa_title: Analyze laboratory findings.
rationale: Once findings are digital, correlation and flagging are well within model reach, but clinical or scientific interpretation that drives consequential decisions needs a credentialed signer.

dwa_title: Analyze biological samples.
rationale: Automated liquid handling and assay platforms cover routine sample processing, but preparation of non-standard samples and troubleshooting anomalous runs still demand bench hands and expert oversight.

dwa_title: Analyze chemical compounds or substances.
rationale: Automated analyzers and chemometric software handle instrument runs and spectral matching, but sample preparation, handling and method selection remain hands-on in a lab, and results affecting safety or regulatory compliance need a signing analyst.

dwa_title: Analyze financial information.
rationale: Purely symbolic work over structured and textual data that models handle well; the binding constraint is data trustworthiness and the fact that material financial conclusions are attested to by a named professional.

dwa_title: Analyze business or financial data.
rationale: BI pipelines plus LLM analysis can generate most descriptive and diagnostic findings; framing the business question and owning the interpretation for decision-makers is what still requires a human.

dwa_title: Conduct quantitative failure analyses of operational data.
rationale: Reliability statistics (Weibull fits, Pareto/root-cause ranking) are well-codified and scriptable, but linking statistical signal to true physical failure mechanisms needs engineering knowledge of the asset and carries safety accountability.

dwa_title: Analyze security of systems, network, or data.
rationale: Scanners, SIEM correlation and increasingly LLM triage automate detection breadth, but adversarial novelty, false-positive arbitration and risk acceptance decisions keep a named security owner in the loop.

dwa_title: Interpret design or operational test results.
rationale: Models can compute against spec limits and draft interpretations, but deciding whether anomalous results mean a design flaw, a test artifact or an acceptable deviation is contested engineering judgment that must be signed off.

dwa_title: Analyze test or validation data.
rationale: Pass/fail checking against defined acceptance criteria is already automated in test benches and validation suites; the residual human role is adjudicating out-of-spec and ambiguous cases and attesting to validation.

dwa_title: Analyze test or performance data to assess equipment operation.
rationale: Condition-monitoring and predictive-maintenance platforms already flag equipment degradation from sensor streams with little human input; interpretation becomes human only when the recommended action is costly or safety-critical.

dwa_title: Estimate costs or terms of sales.
rationale: CPQ and dynamic pricing engines already generate quotes and terms automatically for standardised offerings; bespoke deals hinge on reading the customer and on commitment authority a human holds.

dwa_title: Determine causes of operational problems or failures.
rationale: Root-cause reasoning is language-tractable when data is complete, but causes usually surface only through on-site inspection, interviewing operators and physically probing the system, which no deployed system does end-to-end.

dwa_title: Troubleshoot equipment or systems operation problems.
rationale: Troubleshooting is an interactive loop of hypothesis, physical test and reconfiguration on the equipment itself; automated diagnostics assist the hypothesis step but cannot execute the manipulation.

dwa_title: Diagnose equipment malfunctions.
rationale: Onboard fault codes and diagnostic software narrow the field, but confirming a malfunction requires sensory and manual access to the machine — disassembly, measurement, listening and feeling — that remains human.

dwa_title: Approve expenditures.
rationale: Rule-based spend approvals are already auto-approved below thresholds, but fiduciary and audit requirements demand a named authorizer with delegated signing authority for anything discretionary.

dwa_title: Determine appropriate methods for data analysis.
rationale: Selecting statistical or modelling approaches is pure reasoning over data structure and question framing, which LLMs and AutoML do well; the constraint is that method choice encodes contestable assumptions a domain expert must defend.

dwa_title: Determine protocols for medical procedures.
rationale: Models can synthesise guidelines and draft protocol text, but clinical protocols require licensed physician sign-off and institutional review because patient safety liability is non-delegable.

dwa_title: Determine operational methods.
rationale: Highly heterogeneous activity; optimisation software already sets many operational parameters, but choosing methods usually requires tacit knowledge of the specific worksite and buy-in from those who will execute them.

dwa_title: Determine methods to minimize environmental impact of activities.
rationale: Regulatory synthesis and mitigation-option generation are strongly LLM-exposed, but the tradeoffs among cost, ecology and compliance are contested and permits require a certified professional's attestation.

dwa_title: Diagnose dental conditions.
rationale: Caries and radiograph AI detection is commercially deployed, but diagnosis still needs intraoral examination, tactile probing and a licensed dentist to own the finding.

dwa_title: Diagnose medical conditions.
rationale: Frontier models match or beat clinicians on vignette reasoning, yet physical examination, history elicitation and statutory licensure mean the diagnostic act legally belongs to a named clinician.

dwa_title: Diagnose neural or psychological disorders.
rationale: Psychiatric and neuropsychological diagnosis rests on clinical observation of affect and behaviour within a therapeutic relationship, with contested criteria and licensure-bound liability.

dwa_title: Edit written materials.
