rationale: Text revision for grammar, clarity and style is the canonical LLM strength and is already shipped in mainstream writing tools; only high-stakes voice and factual verification still pull a human back in.

dwa_title: Edit documents.
rationale: Document editing is language transformation over supplied text, fully within deployed model capability; residual human need is limited to final responsibility for contractual or regulated wording.

dwa_title: Estimate technical or resource requirements for development or production projects.
rationale: Parametric estimating software plus models can generate resource takeoffs quickly, but the binding constraint is unmodelled project-specific scope uncertainty that an estimator must judge and stand behind in a bid.

dwa_title: Estimate time requirements for development or production projects.
rationale: Historical-data-driven schedule estimation is well suited to algorithms and already embedded in project tools, yet novel scope, dependency risk and organisational optimism require human calibration and commitment.

dwa_title: Determine types of equipment, tools, or materials needed for jobs.
rationale: Specifying equipment and materials is codified knowledge work that estimating software and LLMs handle well from specs, but binding constraint is tacit site/job knowledge and the fact that a wrong bill of materials creates real downstream cost, so a qualified human signs off.

dwa_title: Identify information technology project resource requirements.
rationale: Almost entirely document- and data-based reasoning that models do strongly, but accurate IT resourcing depends on undocumented organizational context, stakeholder negotiation and commitments that a named project owner must make.

dwa_title: Determine resource needs.
rationale: Generic resource determination is analytic and highly model-exposed, but the input assumptions are rarely fully documented and the resulting budget commitment is owned by a human manager; wording is too broad for a confident call.

dwa_title: Estimate supplies, ingredients, or staff requirements for food preparation activities.
rationale: Demand forecasting and par-level software already computes ingredient and labor needs from POS history; the residual human role is correcting for local events, deliveries and on-hand stock that the system cannot observe.

dwa_title: Implement organizational process or policy changes.
rationale: Implementation, as opposed to drafting, is change management: securing buy-in, exercising authority over staff and absorbing resistance, none of which can be delegated to a system that no one reports to.

dwa_title: Apply new technologies to improve work processes.
rationale: Models can identify and configure candidate technologies, but actually inserting them into a live workflow requires physical/system integration and retraining people, which stalls end-to-end automation.

dwa_title: Implement advertising or marketing initiatives.
rationale: Programmatic ad platforms plus generative creative already execute large parts of campaign launch and optimization; the constraint is brand, budget and legal approval plus coordination with agencies and channel partners.

dwa_title: Implement design or process improvements.
rationale: Designing the improvement is model-tractable but putting it into production touches equipment, procedures and people on the floor, and a responsible engineer or supervisor must validate the changed process.

dwa_title: Select tools, equipment, or technologies for use in operations or projects.
rationale: Matching specifications to catalogued tool and technology options is well within model capability; procurement authority and fitness-for-purpose liability keep the final selection with a human.

dwa_title: Select educational materials or equipment.
rationale: Content matching to standards and learner level is strongly model-exposed, but adoption decisions carry pedagogical judgment about specific students and are subject to district or parental accountability.

dwa_title: Select resources needed to accomplish tasks.
rationale: An abstract allocation decision that maps well onto model reasoning and optimization tools; ambiguity of the phrasing and reliance on unlogged local availability limit full automation.

dwa_title: Select project materials.
rationale: Material selection against performance, code and cost criteria is highly analyzable, but samples are often judged in hand and specification errors carry warranty or code-compliance liability requiring a named specifier.

dwa_title: Select production input materials.
rationale: ERP/MRP and supplier-optimisation systems already automate routine input selection against specs and cost, but the binding constraint is verifying actual material quality and supply-chain tradeoffs that require physical inspection and vendor negotiation.

dwa_title: Select medical equipment for addressing patient needs.
rationale: Matching equipment to a specific patient's anatomy, function and tolerance requires in-person assessment and fitting, and a licensed clinician must own the selection for safety and liability reasons.

dwa_title: Develop treatment plans for patients or clients.
rationale: Models can draft coherent, guideline-consistent plans, but licensure and duty-of-care mean a named professional must author and sign the plan, and plan quality depends on relational elicitation of the client's goals and constraints.

dwa_title: Develop medical treatment plans.
rationale: Medical treatment planning is squarely within LLM reasoning reach as drafting, yet prescribing authority and malpractice liability legally bind the decision to a licensed physician.

dwa_title: Develop exercise or conditioning programs.
rationale: Commercial fitness and rehab apps already generate individualised conditioning programs algorithmically; what still requires a human is screening for contraindications and adjusting to observed movement quality.

dwa_title: Modify treatment plans to accommodate client needs.
rationale: The substance is negotiating adherence, preferences and life circumstances with the client, and any deviation from the standard plan must be justified by an accountable practitioner.

dwa_title: Develop treatment plans that use non-medical therapies.
rationale: Non-medical therapeutic planning rests on a sustained therapeutic alliance and weakly codified evidence, so the practitioner's read of the person, not information retrieval, is the limiting input.

dwa_title: Establish treatment goals.
rationale: Goal-setting is a collaborative act of eliciting and calibrating a patient's own aspirations against clinical realism; the shared commitment is the deliverable and cannot be outsourced to a system.

dwa_title: Develop software or computer applications.
rationale: Code generation is the strongest current LLM capability and agentic tools now complete whole features, but requirement ambiguity, integration with legacy context and review for correctness still gate end-to-end autonomy.

dwa_title: Design software applications.
rationale: Architectural design involves contested tradeoffs over cost, scale and maintainability elicited from stakeholders; models produce credible design options but cannot resolve which organisational constraints dominate.

dwa_title: Design healthcare-related software applications.
rationale: Same design reasoning as general software but bound by HIPAA, safety-critical validation and device regulation, which require a named human to attest to design controls.

dwa_title: Apply information technology to solve business or other applied problems.
rationale: Translating a messy business problem into a technical solution is heavily LLM-assisted in analysis and prototyping, but the binding constraint is diagnosing the real organisational problem with stakeholders who state it imprecisely.

dwa_title: Develop computer or information systems.
rationale: Coding agents now generate and integrate substantial system components, but eliciting requirements from stakeholders and owning architectural trade-offs across a live organisation still requires a human to hold the thread.

dwa_title: Design computer modeling or simulation programs.
rationale: The binding constraint is validation: models write simulation code fluently but cannot certify that the abstraction faithfully represents the modelled physical or economic system.

dwa_title: Develop computer or online applications.
rationale: Greenfield application code is the single most automatable knowledge task today; what still fails is sustained autonomy over integration, ambiguous specs and production consequences.

dwa_title: Design integrated computer systems.
rationale: Integration design depends on undocumented legacy interfaces, vendor constraints and hardware realities that a model cannot inspect or negotiate on its own.

dwa_title: Develop software or applications for scientific or technical use.
rationale: Scientific software is textual and highly LLM-exposed, but correctness must be anchored to domain theory and experimental ground truth that only the responsible researcher can attest to.

dwa_title: Modify software programs to improve performance.
rationale: Profiling data plus code gives a closed feedback loop that models exploit well; the limit is regression risk in large unfamiliar codebases, which still needs human review before merge.

dwa_title: Design websites or web applications.
rationale: Template and generative site builders already ship end-to-end for commodity cases; bespoke brand, accessibility and conversion judgment is what keeps a designer in the loop.

dwa_title: Design video game features or details.
rationale: Game feel is validated by iterative playtesting against human taste, an evaluation signal models cannot generate internally even though they ideate and prototype quickly.

dwa_title: Develop marketing plans or strategies.
rationale: Models draft credible strategy from data, but committing budget requires reading internal politics and betting on contested assumptions about competitor and consumer response.

dwa_title: Create new recipes or food presentations.
rationale: Taste, aroma and plating must be iterated by a body in a kitchen; text generation can only propose combinations it cannot evaluate.

dwa_title: Plan menu options.
rationale: Menu planning is largely constraint optimisation over cost, seasonality and demand data that software handles well, but final selection depends on tasted quality and local clientele knowledge.

dwa_title: Develop healthcare quality and safety procedures.
rationale: Drafting protocol text is highly model-exposed, but regulators and accreditation bodies require a named clinical leader to approve procedures on which patient safety depends.

dwa_title: Develop safety standards, policies, or procedures.
rationale: Drafting standards text is highly tractable for language models, but the binding constraint is that safety policy must be adopted and signed by an accountable officer with knowledge of site-specific hazards and regulatory exposure.

dwa_title: Establish rules or policies governing student behavior.
rationale: Model can generate conduct codes, but legitimacy with students, parents and school boards depends on a named educator's authority and relational standing, which cannot be delegated to software.

dwa_title: Develop fire safety or prevention programs or plans.
rationale: Fire plans follow codified codes that LLMs handle well, but they require on-site inspection of building conditions and sign-off by a licensed fire protection professional or marshal.

dwa_title: Develop database parameters or specifications.
rationale: Schema and parameter design is pure symbolic work well within model capability; the constraint is eliciting real business requirements and owning downstream performance and migration consequences.

dwa_title: Develop technical or scientific databases.
rationale: Model-generated DDL and ingestion code is already practical, but domain-specific data semantics, provenance and curation decisions still require a scientist's involvement.

dwa_title: Create databases to store electronic data.
rationale: Instantiating a database from a specification is scripted, reversible and routinely handled by templates, provisioning tools and code-generating assistants.

dwa_title: Plan natural resources conservation or restoration programs.
rationale: Conservation planning hinges on contested ecological judgment, field reconnaissance and negotiation among landowners, agencies and stakeholders rather than on document production.

dwa_title: Develop environmental remediation or protection plans.
rationale: Remediation plans are regulatory documents that must be stamped by a licensed engineer or geologist and rest on site characterisation data gathered in the field.

dwa_title: Develop environmental sustainability plans or projects.
rationale: Sustainability planning is largely analysis and narrative synthesis that models do well, but target-setting requires organisational buy-in and executive ownership of commitments.

dwa_title: Develop plans to manage natural or renewable resources.
rationale: Resource management plans depend on locally observed stock conditions and irreducibly contested trade-offs among competing users, with statutory decision authority resting on an agency official.

dwa_title: Develop health assessment methods or programs.
rationale: Designing screening instruments and programs is evidence-synthesis work suited to models, but clinical validity and population impact require accountable licensed health professionals.

dwa_title: Develop promotional materials.
rationale: Generative text and image tools already produce deployable promotional copy and creative at scale; the residual human role is brand judgment and legal review, and errors are cheap to correct.

dwa_title: Develop content for sales presentations or other materials.
rationale: Generating persuasive copy, decks and supporting collateral from product and customer data is squarely what generative models already do end-to-end; the binding constraint is only access to accurate internal product/pricing facts and brand sign-off.

dwa_title: Design materials for industrial or commercial applications.
rationale: Computational materials design and generative simulation tools accelerate candidate generation, but selection still hinges on physical synthesis, characterisation and failure testing that no deployed system closes the loop on.

dwa_title: Design micro- or nano-scale materials, devices, or systems.
rationale: Nanoscale design is bound by fabrication constraints and process-specific tacit knowledge discovered in cleanroom iteration; models help with parameter search and literature synthesis but cannot own the design-fabricate-measure cycle.

dwa_title: Design medical devices or appliances.
rationale: Regulatory design-control regimes require a named engineer accountable for risk analysis and verification of a device that can kill a patient, so even excellent AI-generated designs must be owned by a qualified human.

dwa_title: Establish work standards.
rationale: Drafting standards from observed process data is well within model capability, but the standard only binds if a manager with authority negotiates and ratifies it with the workforce.

dwa_title: Design psychological or educational treatment procedures or programs.
rationale: Treatment protocol design sits inside clinical licensure and duty of care; a licensed practitioner must own the diagnostic formulation and the risk of harm even when a model drafts the protocol.

dwa_title: Develop instructional objectives.
rationale: Writing measurable objectives aligned to standards and taxonomies is a highly templated text task that current models perform reliably; only local curricular approval remains human.

dwa_title: Plan experiential learning activities.
rationale: Ideas and lesson scaffolds generate easily, but experiential activities depend on site logistics, safety supervision and knowledge of the specific learner group, which requires a present organiser.

dwa_title: Establish operational policies.
rationale: Policy text can be drafted and benchmarked by models, but issuing policy is an exercise of delegated organisational authority with legal exposure that must rest with an identified officer.

dwa_title: Develop strategies or programs for students with special needs.
rationale: Special-needs planning is statutorily governed (IEP-type processes) and built from direct observation of the child plus negotiation with families and specialists, so a credentialed human must author and be answerable for it.

dwa_title: Develop educational programs.
rationale: Curriculum architecture, sequencing and materials are strongly model-assisted, but fitting a program to institutional constraints, accreditation and real learner populations requires a human owner.

dwa_title: Develop educational or training programs.
rationale: Needs analysis and content build-out are highly text-based and already tooled, yet stakeholder alignment on what the training must achieve and compliance sign-off keep a human in the lead.

dwa_title: Design water conservation systems.
rationale: Hydrologic modelling and design software can generate options, but site-specific constraints, regulatory sign-off and stakeholder water rights require a responsible engineer; the binding constraint is professional accountability for a physically deployed system.

dwa_title: Apply knowledge or research findings to address environmental problems.
rationale: Synthesising literature and mapping findings onto a problem is core LLM territory, but translating research into a defensible intervention under ecological uncertainty and contested evidence still needs an accountable expert.

dwa_title: Protect wildlife or natural areas.
rationale: Protection is enacted in the field through habitat management, enforcement and negotiation with landowners; sensing and monitoring can be automated but the protective action itself is embodied and legally attributed.

dwa_title: Design environmental control systems.
rationale: Parametric and simulation tools automate large parts of HVAC/emission control system sizing, but code compliance and stamped engineering drawings bind the work to a licensed human.

dwa_title: Design energy-efficient vehicles or vehicle components.
rationale: Generative design and CFD/FEA optimisation accelerate component design, but prototyping, validation testing and safety homologation keep engineers in ownership of the outcome.

dwa_title: Design alternative energy systems.
rationale: Solar/wind layout and sizing software already automates much of the configuration, but site assessment, grid interconnection approval and a stamped design require a licensed engineer.

dwa_title: Design systems to reduce harmful emissions.
rationale: Emissions-control design is heavily model-assisted, but regulatory certification and liability for exceedances legally anchor responsibility to a named engineer.

dwa_title: Design energy-efficient equipment or systems.
rationale: Energy modelling and optimisation tools handle much of the trade-off analysis; the constraint is physical validation and code-compliant sign-off rather than cognitive difficulty.

dwa_title: Plan programs to address community health issues.
rationale: Needs assessment and program drafting are text-heavy and LLM-amenable, but community buy-in, coalition building and public accountability for health outcomes make the relationship the substance of the work.

dwa_title: Design public or employee health programs.
rationale: Program design documents can be largely drafted by a model against evidence-based guidelines, but organisational negotiation, privacy/legal compliance and ownership of participant outcomes require a human sponsor.

dwa_title: Prepare drawings or diagrams of products or services.
rationale: Generative image and diagramming tools already produce usable illustrative drawings from specifications; the remaining constraint is fidelity to client intent and technical accuracy checking rather than accountability.

dwa_title: Create diagrams or blueprints for workpieces or products.
rationale: CAD automation and model-based definition can generate dimensioned drawings from parametric models, but tolerance decisions and manufacturability sign-off still attach to a drafter or engineer because errors propagate into scrapped parts.

dwa_title: Prepare maps.
rationale: GIS pipelines already auto-generate styled cartography from spatial databases; the binding constraint is source-data validation and cartographic design choices for a particular audience, which still needs a human editor.

dwa_title: Develop diagrams or flow charts of system operation.
rationale: Diagramming is essentially structured text (Mermaid, PlantUML, BPMN) that frontier models generate reliably; the only real limit is accurately eliciting how the undocumented system actually behaves.

dwa_title: Prepare graphics or other visual representations of information.
rationale: Chart and infographic generation from data is a solved code-generation problem with deployed tooling; residual human role is taste and checking that the visual does not mislead.

dwa_title: Draw detailed or technical illustrations.
rationale: Generative imaging cannot hold dimensional and part-level precision, so technical illustration still runs through human-driven CAD/vector work; models mainly accelerate layout, callouts and variants.

dwa_title: Create graphical representations of structures or landscapes.
rationale: Rendering engines and diffusion models produce convincing structure and landscape visuals cheaply, but fidelity to the actual designed geometry and site conditions requires a human driving the model.

dwa_title: Create graphical representations of mechanical equipment.
rationale: Parametric CAD automates derivative views and drawing sheets from a model, but authoring the geometry itself with correct tolerances and manufacturability remains human-led.

dwa_title: Create maps.
rationale: Automated map compilation from geospatial layers is routine, yet decisions about projection, generalisation and what to omit carry interpretive weight a human still owns.

dwa_title: Create images or other visual displays.
rationale: Generic image and visual-display creation is precisely what deployed generative models do end-to-end; only client intent and rights clearance keep a person in the loop.

dwa_title: Create graphical representations of industrial production systems.
rationale: Plant layouts and P&IDs must encode verified process logic and safety interlocks, so drafting software accelerates production while an engineer remains the source of truth and the signatory.

dwa_title: Create graphical representations of civil structures.
rationale: BIM and detailing tools generate large parts of the drawing set, but civil drawings are permit instruments requiring a licensed engineer's seal, which anchors responsibility to a person.

dwa_title: Create electrical schematics.
rationale: EDA tools already auto-generate netlists, symbols and routing, and models can draft standard circuits, but code-compliant and safe topology selection still requires qualified human sign-off.

dwa_title: Create graphical representations of energy production systems.
rationale: Single-line diagrams and plant schematics for energy systems feed directly into regulated safety and grid-interconnection review, so drafting is assisted but ownership stays with a licensed engineer.

dwa_title: Create schematic drawings for electronics.
rationale: EDA tools already automate symbol placement, netlist checks and routing, and models can draft circuit topologies from specs, but binding constraint is that correct component selection and manufacturability still require an engineer to verify and sign off before fabrication.

dwa_title: Design layout of art or product exhibits, displays, or promotional materials.
rationale: Generative image and layout tools can produce strong concept options, but the design must be resolved against a real physical space, sightlines and materials, and client taste negotiation anchors the final call to a human.

dwa_title: Develop emergency procedures.
rationale: Drafting procedures against codes and hazard scenarios is highly text-tractable, but emergency plans must be validated against a specific site and are legally attributable to a named safety officer or authority having jurisdiction.

dwa_title: Maintain contingency plans for disaster recovery.
rationale: Plan upkeep is largely document reconciliation against changing systems and can be substantially machine-drafted, but currency of the plan depends on tacit knowledge of real dependencies and someone must attest that recovery will actually work.

dwa_title: Develop operating strategies, plans, or procedures for green or sustainable operations.
rationale: Benchmarking practices and writing strategy documents is squarely in model capability, but the binding constraint is securing organizational buy-in and trading off cost against environmental goals in a contested internal setting.

dwa_title: Develop sustainable organizational policies or practices.
rationale: Policy text generation is a near-ideal language task, but policy only exists once negotiated and adopted by accountable leadership, which is a relational and governance act rather than a drafting one.

dwa_title: Develop sustainable industrial or development methods.
rationale: Designing genuinely new industrial or development methods requires empirical validation in physical process conditions; models can propose and screen options but cannot close the loop on whether a method works at scale.

dwa_title: Develop operational methods or processes that use green materials or emphasize sustainability.
rationale: Material substitution can be screened from databases and literature by models, but performance, durability and regulatory compliance of the substitute must be proven through physical testing in the actual process.

dwa_title: Devise research or testing protocols.
rationale: Protocol writing is structured reasoning over prior literature and standards where models perform well, but the design choices carry validity and safety consequences requiring review boards and a responsible investigator.

dwa_title: Develop biological research methods.
rationale: Method development in biology is iterative wet-lab troubleshooting where tacit bench knowledge and physical trial dominate; models accelerate literature-based design but cannot run the optimization loop.

dwa_title: Develop methods of social or economic research.
rationale: Survey instruments, sampling frames and identification strategies are pure information work that frontier models handle well; the constraint is contested methodological judgment that peers must be able to challenge and a researcher must defend.

dwa_title: Design research studies to obtain scientific information.
rationale: Study design is reasoning over confounds, power and feasibility that models can draft competently, but the choice of what question is worth asking and the ethical/scientific warrant for the design remain attributed to a named investigator.

dwa_title: Plan biological research.
rationale: Models can draft hypotheses, designs, protocols and power calculations from the literature, but the binding constraint is that a named investigator must own feasibility, ethics approval and resource commitments for work involving living systems.

dwa_title: Plan environmental research.
rationale: Study design and sampling strategy are text-and-analysis work an LLM handles well, but site conditions, regulatory scope and stakeholder negotiation force a responsible human planner.

dwa_title: Develop environmental research methods.
rationale: Devising novel sampling and measurement methods requires validating them against messy field reality and instrument behaviour, which no deployed system can close the loop on.

dwa_title: Plan social sciences research.
rationale: Instrument design, sampling frames and analysis plans are almost purely textual and statistical, so LLM leverage is high; human-subjects ethics review requires a named principal investigator.

dwa_title: Develop theories or models of physical phenomena.
rationale: Frontier models manipulate formalism and derive consequences competently, but genuinely novel theory construction still depends on human taste about which abstraction is worth pursuing and on empirical confrontation.

dwa_title: Develop mathematical models of environmental conditions.
rationale: Model fitting, calibration and code generation are heavily tooled and partly automated already; the residual human role is choosing structural assumptions and defending predictions used in regulation or risk decisions.

dwa_title: Develop scientific or mathematical models.
rationale: This is essentially symbolic and computational reasoning where LLMs plus solvers are strongest; validation against reality and assumption selection remain the human-held step.

dwa_title: Develop theories or models of social phenomena.
rationale: Social theorising is pure discursive reasoning and hence maximally LLM-exposed, but contestability of interpretation and the need for scholarly ownership of claims keep a human at the centre.

dwa_title: Develop program goals or plans.
rationale: Drafting goals and plans is easy for a model, but goals bind budgets and staff and therefore require legitimacy conferred by an accountable leader negotiating with stakeholders.

dwa_title: Develop organizational goals or objectives.
rationale: Setting organisational direction is an act of authority and commitment; even a perfect draft must be owned by executives or a board who answer to stakeholders for it.

dwa_title: Review professional literature to maintain professional knowledge.
rationale: Retrieval, screening and summarisation of literature is already well served by deployed tools; the constraint is that the resulting knowledge must be internalised by the practitioner who will later apply it.

dwa_title: Research topics in area of expertise.
rationale: Information gathering and synthesis is the archetypal LLM task with search tools; residual risk of fabricated or stale sources means an expert must verify before relying on the output.

dwa_title: Maintain medical or professional knowledge.
rationale: Literature surveillance, summarisation and guideline tracking are strongly LLM-exposed, but the binding constraint is that the competence must reside in the licensed clinician who will act on it and be answerable for outdated practice.

dwa_title: Conduct research to inform art, designs, or other work.
rationale: Reference gathering, visual and textual precedent search are precisely what retrieval-augmented models do well; what limits full automation is that the researcher's aesthetic intent shapes what counts as relevant material, and some source material must be experienced in situ.

dwa_title: Maintain knowledge of laws or regulations.
rationale: Regulatory horizon-scanning services already ingest and summarise rule changes automatically, but interpreting applicability to a specific operation and bearing compliance liability keeps a named professional in the loop.

dwa_title: Maintain professional knowledge or certifications.
rationale: Credentialing bodies attach certification to an identified individual who must personally complete and pass continuing-education requirements; the credential cannot be delegated to a machine regardless of how well it knows the material.

dwa_title: Attend training sessions or professional meetings to develop or maintain professional knowledge.
rationale: Attendance is itself the deliverable — credit hours and peer contact are credited to a present person; models can summarise proceedings but cannot substitute for the attendee.

dwa_title: Update technical knowledge.
rationale: Technical documentation, release notes and standards are ideal LLM input, yet much technical currency is acquired through hands-on practice with the equipment or system and must be internalised by the practitioner.

dwa_title: Update professional knowledge.
rationale: Machines can curate and digest the source material at scale, but the purpose of the activity is to install knowledge in the human who will later exercise it unaided.

dwa_title: Study product information to acquire professional knowledge.
rationale: Ingesting spec sheets and product literature is near-pure document comprehension, highly amenable to models; the constraint is that the worker must be able to recall and apply it live in front of a customer or on a job.

dwa_title: Stay informed about current developments in field of specialization.
rationale: Automated alerting and summarisation pipelines already deliver field developments continuously; judging which developments matter for one's own practice, and absorbing them, remains the human's part.

dwa_title: Attend events to develop professional knowledge.
rationale: The value lies in bodily presence and professional networking at the event; no system can attend on a person's behalf even though it can digest the published content afterwards.

dwa_title: Maintain current knowledge related to work activities.
rationale: Heterogeneous activity spanning document reading and hands-on familiarity; tools can supply the information stream but the knowledge must end up in the worker performing the downstream tasks.

dwa_title: Update knowledge about emerging industry or technology trends.
rationale: Trend monitoring is largely automated scanning and synthesis of public information, but distinguishing durable signal from hype is a contested judgment call the human still owns.

dwa_title: Maintain knowledge of current developments in area of expertise.
rationale: Monitoring and digesting literature, standards and news is exactly what retrieval-plus-LLM pipelines do well, but the output is an internalised competence a licensed or accountable practitioner must actually hold and apply, not a deliverable a machine can own.

dwa_title: Attend conferences or workshops to maintain professional knowledge.
rationale: The binding constraint is that attendance itself, including the networking and CE-credit attestation tied to a named individual, cannot be delegated; only the note-taking and summarising slice is machine-substitutable.

dwa_title: Develop organizational policies or programs.
rationale: Drafting policy text and benchmarking against precedent is highly LLM-exposed, but policy creation requires negotiating stakeholder interests and carries legal and governance liability that an identified officer or board must accept.

dwa_title: Develop operating strategies, plans, or procedures.
rationale: Strategy and operating plans rest on contested assumptions about an organisation's future and require buy-in from those who must execute them; models accelerate option generation and documentation but cannot commit the organisation.

dwa_title: Develop organizational methods or procedures.
rationale: Procedure and method design is largely document work that LLMs draft competently, but fitting it to tacit local workflow realities and signing off on compliance keeps a human owner.

dwa_title: Schedule medical facility use.
rationale: Room, theatre and equipment booking is a constrained optimisation already handled by deployed hospital scheduling systems; the residual human role is exception handling when clinical urgency overrides the algorithm.

dwa_title: Schedule activities or facility use.
rationale: Generic facility and activity booking is a solved calendaring and resource-allocation problem with mature commercial software; only contested priority calls need a person.

dwa_title: Schedule instructional activities.
rationale: Timetabling engines already solve room, instructor and cohort constraints; the friction is negotiating instructor preferences and pedagogical sequencing, which is small relative to the combinatorial core.

dwa_title: Schedule operational activities.
rationale: Operational scheduling is the canonical domain of deployed planning and workforce-management software; human input mainly enters when shifting priorities or staffing disputes break the model's assumptions.

dwa_title: Schedule appointments.
rationale: Self-service booking platforms and voice/chat agents already complete appointment scheduling end-to-end; nothing in the task requires a human signature.

dwa_title: Schedule patient procedures or appointments.
rationale: Patient self-scheduling is widely deployed, but procedure booking involves clinical prerequisites, prep instructions and urgency triage where a misordered slot carries real patient harm, so oversight persists.

dwa_title: Plan special events.
rationale: Itineraries, budgets and vendor shortlists are readily machine-drafted, but the binding work is negotiating with suppliers and clients and being on site when contingencies hit.

dwa_title: Plan community programs or activities for the general public.
rationale: An LLM can draft program concepts, schedules and outreach materials, but the binding constraint is reading local community needs and coordinating stakeholders, sponsors and venues in person.

dwa_title: Plan work operations.
rationale: Scheduling and workload allocation are well served by optimization tools and LLM drafting, but committing people to work requires authority over staff and tacit knowledge of local constraints.

dwa_title: Prepare detailed work plans.
rationale: The output is a structured document, squarely within LLM capability; what stops full automation is dependence on undocumented site and resource realities and the need for a manager to own the plan.

dwa_title: Develop detailed project plans.
rationale: Project plans are text plus dependency logic that models and PM software generate well; the constraint is negotiating scope and resources with stakeholders and accountability for schedule and budget commitments.

dwa_title: Plan production or operational procedures or sequences.
rationale: Production sequencing is a mature domain for APS and scheduling optimizers, but equipment quirks, quality and safety consequences keep a process engineer signing off.

dwa_title: Prepare medications or medical solutions.
rationale: Robotic IV compounders and pharmacy automation exist, yet physical handling plus licensure-based responsibility for a dose that can kill a patient keeps a named pharmacist or nurse accountable.

dwa_title: Protect property from fire or water damage.
rationale: Sprinklers and shutoff systems automate fixed cases, but salvage and protective action in an unstructured emergency scene demands bodily presence and improvisation no deployed robot provides.

dwa_title: Maintain clean work areas.
rationale: Floor-scrubbing robots handle open surfaces only; clearing clutter, wiping surfaces and tidying tools require dexterous manipulation in cluttered space that is not commercially solved.

dwa_title: Clean equipment, parts, or tools to repair or maintain them in good working order.
rationale: Automated parts washers cover batch cleaning, but disassembly and targeted cleaning of varied tools and components is dexterity-bound.

dwa_title: Decontaminate equipment or sites to remove hazardous or toxic substances.
rationale: Remote-handling equipment assists in hot zones, but regulated hazmat decontamination requires certified personnel physically on site and answerable for clearance verification.

dwa_title: Clean facilities or equipment.
rationale: Clean-in-place systems and floor robots automate specific slices; general cleaning of arbitrary facilities and machines remains a manipulation problem.

dwa_title: Clean facilities or work areas.
rationale: Commercial cleaning robots cover large uncluttered floors but not detail work around fixtures and objects, so human hands remain the binding requirement.

dwa_title: Dispose of hazardous materials.
rationale: Handling and manifesting hazardous waste is physically in-situ and legally regulated with named responsible parties; only the classification and documentation layer is machine-assistable.

dwa_title: Dispose of trash or waste materials.
rationale: Automated bin lifts and some warehouse waste handling exist, but general trash collection across unstructured environments still needs human hands and mobility.

dwa_title: Assist skilled construction or extraction personnel.
rationale: Ad hoc physical helping on a changing worksite, coordinated in real time with a tradesperson, is far beyond deployed robotics.

dwa_title: Clean objects.
rationale: Industrial parts washers and cleaning machines automate the repetitive cases, but arbitrary objects and surfaces still require dexterous human handling.

dwa_title: Sterilize medical equipment or instruments.
rationale: Autoclaves and washer-disinfectors do the sterilization itself, but loading, inspection, packaging and validated sign-off of sterility remain a human responsibility.

dwa_title: Clean medical equipment or facilities.
rationale: UV robots and floor scrubbers cover a fraction; infection-control cleaning of high-touch surfaces in occupied clinical space requires dexterous, judgment-guided human work.

dwa_title: Deliver items.
rationale: Indoor delivery robots and some sidewalk/AV pilots are deployed, but last-metre handoff across varied buildings and recipients still binds humans to the task.

dwa_title: Enforce rules or regulations.
rationale: Detection can be automated, but confronting a person, exercising discretion and bearing legal authority for the enforcement action requires an accountable human.

dwa_title: Maintain security.
rationale: Surveillance analytics and access control are heavily automated, yet physical response to incidents and liability for safety outcomes keep a human on post.

dwa_title: Provide escort or transportation.
rationale: Being bodily present with and responsible for the safety of the person escorted is the substance of the task; driverless transport does not supply the escorting function.

dwa_title: Accompany patients or clients on outings to provide assistance.
rationale: Duty of care for a vulnerable person in an unpredictable public setting is inherently relational and embodied.

dwa_title: Accompany individuals or groups to activities.
rationale: Supervising and being physically alongside people during activities is a presence-and-responsibility role no deployed system can assume.

dwa_title: Move patients to or from treatment areas.
rationale: Safe physical transfer of a fragile, variably cooperative human body in cluttered clinical spaces is beyond deployed robotics; reassurance and patient-safety accountability travel with the person doing the lifting.

dwa_title: Practice athletic or artistic skills.
rationale: The activity is the embodied human development of skill itself — the point is that a specific human body improves, so substitution is conceptually impossible even if coaching analytics can assist.

dwa_title: Cultivate land.
rationale: Auto-steer tractors and GPS-guided tillage are commercially real and among the most automated field operations, but supervision, hitching, and field-edge decisions still keep an operator in or near the cab.

dwa_title: Install safety or support equipment.
rationale: Installing shoring, guardrails or fall-protection on unstructured worksites demands dexterous in-situ work plus a competent person legally signing off on safety adequacy.

dwa_title: Fabricate devices or components.
rationale: High-volume fabrication is automated, but the generic activity spans one-off and custom assembly where fixturing, fitting and part variability still require human hands.

dwa_title: Fabricate products or components using machine tools.
rationale: CNC machining with automated tool changers and pallet loading is mature and CAM programming is increasingly model-assisted; setup, workholding, inspection and troubleshooting still bind a machinist to the cell.

dwa_title: Apply chemical solutions to plants to protect against disease or insects or to enhance growth.
rationale: Autonomous sprayers and see-and-spray systems are deployed in row crops, but licensed applicator responsibility for pesticide use, drift and dosage keeps a certified human accountable.

dwa_title: Stock products or parts.
rationale: Warehouse goods-to-person robotics handle replenishment in engineered facilities, but shelf-level stocking of heterogeneous items in retail environments remains a dexterity problem unsolved at scale.

dwa_title: Stock medical or patient care supplies.
rationale: Automated dispensing cabinets and par-level software cover the tracking layer, but physically restocking varied clinical supplies in occupied care areas, with sterility and expiry checks, stays manual.

dwa_title: Collect biological specimens from patients.
rationale: Venipuncture robots remain unadopted; identity verification, consent, patient anxiety management and chain-of-custody liability require a licensed human at the bedside.

dwa_title: Collect biological specimens.
rationale: Automated samplers and drone/ROV collection exist for some environmental biological sampling, but selecting representative sites and handling irregular specimens without contamination remains hands-on.

dwa_title: Collect geographical or geological field data.
rationale: Remote sensing, drones and instrumented logging capture much field data automatically, yet outcrop interpretation, sample selection and terrain access still require a geoscientist on site.

dwa_title: Collect environmental data or samples.
rationale: Fixed automated sensor stations and autonomous samplers exist for routine monitoring, but most environmental sampling requires travelling to unstructured terrain and physically handling media, which no deployed robot does generally; chain-of-custody signatures add a human anchor.

dwa_title: Package materials for transport.
rationale: Automated case packers, palletisers and shrink-wrappers are mature commercial technology; the constraint is capital cost and product variety, not capability.

dwa_title: Package materials or products.
rationale: High-throughput packaging lines are routinely fully automated; irregular, fragile or low-volume mixed items still defeat deployed grippers, keeping some human packing.

dwa_title: Set up laboratory or field equipment.
rationale: Setup means physically arranging, connecting and calibrating varied apparatus in unstandardised spaces; only fully integrated lab-automation cells do this without hands, and field deployment is wholly manual.

dwa_title: Cultivate micro-organisms for study, testing, or medical preparations.
rationale: Automated incubators, bioreactors and colony-picking robots handle routine culture work, but aseptic technique across varied media and organisms still relies on trained hands, and contamination or misidentification carries real cost.

dwa_title: Prepare biological specimens for laboratory analysis.
rationale: Automated stainers, tissue processors and liquid handlers cover high-volume steps, yet grossing, embedding and irregular specimen handling remain manual and specimen mix-ups have patient-level consequences.

dwa_title: Prepare biological samples for testing or analysis.
rationale: Track-based clinical lab automation already handles centrifugation, aliquoting and loading end-to-end for standard tubes; non-standard sample types and accessioning exceptions keep humans in the loop under licensure.

dwa_title: Prepare compounds or solutions for products or testing.
rationale: Automated dispensing and formulation systems perform routine weighing and dilution reliably; the binding constraint is physical handling of diverse reagents and hazardous materials plus verification of concentration accuracy.

dwa_title: Collect samples for analysis or testing.
rationale: Inline autosamplers automate sampling on fixed process streams, but generalised sampling requires physically reaching varied locations and choosing representative material.

dwa_title: Collect samples of raw materials or finished products.
rationale: Automatic samplers on production lines and silos are commercially common, yet lot-by-lot sampling across warehouses, trucks and batches still needs a person walking to the material.

dwa_title: Assemble mechanical components or machine parts.
rationale: Robotic assembly is fully deployed for high-volume standardised parts, but compliant fitting, fastening and tolerance adjustment in low-volume or complex assemblies still requires human dexterity.

dwa_title: Install gauges or controls.
rationale: Installing instrumentation happens in cramped, one-off equipment configurations requiring manual mounting, wiring and calibration, and a certified technician typically signs off because faulty controls create safety hazards.

dwa_title: Assemble equipment or components.
rationale: High-volume standardized assembly is robot-automated, but the binding constraint is dexterous manipulation of varied parts and fixtures, which remains uneconomic outside high-volume lines.

dwa_title: Reassemble equipment after repair.
rationale: Post-repair reassembly is one-off, unfixtured work on worn or non-uniform units; no deployed robotic system handles this variability.

dwa_title: Assemble precision electronics or optical equipment.
rationale: Pick-and-place and automated optical alignment are mature for mass electronics, but low-volume precision optical assembly still depends on human micro-dexterity and tactile feedback.

dwa_title: Prepare materials for preservation, storage, or display.
rationale: Handling fragile, unique artifacts or specimens requires in-situ tactile care and case-by-case conservation judgment that no deployed system provides.

dwa_title: Adjust tuning or functioning of musical instruments.
rationale: Pitch detection is fully solved by software, but turning pins, voicing and regulating an instrument require skilled hands on the object.

dwa_title: Adjust building climate control systems.
rationale: Building management systems already perform setpoint control and optimization autonomously; only physical valve/damper faults require a technician.

dwa_title: Calibrate scientific or technical equipment.
rationale: Automated calibration routines and drift computation are common, but traceable calibration requires physically connecting standards and a signed certificate from an accredited technician.

dwa_title: Adjust equipment to ensure optimal performance.
rationale: Closed-loop and adaptive control automate parameter tuning where sensors exist, but the generic form covers much hands-on mechanical adjustment with no actuation path.

dwa_title: Calibrate equipment to specifications.
rationale: Calibration against a written spec is rule-bound and increasingly software-driven, yet physical setup and the accountable sign-off keep a technician in the loop.

dwa_title: Adjust settings or positions of medical equipment.
rationale: Positioning equipment relative to a patient's body is embodied and patient-specific, and clinical safety regulation requires a licensed operator to own the setting.

dwa_title: Prepare medical supplies or equipment for use.
rationale: Sterile processing and tray setup involve manipulating diverse instruments under asepsis rules; automation exists only for washing/sterilizing steps, and a named person verifies sterility.

dwa_title: Prepare materials for processing.
rationale: Bulk feeding, batching and dosing are heavily automated in continuous process plants, but non-uniform materials and manual loading in smaller operations still require hands.

dwa_title: Make patient-assistive devices or device models.
rationale: Custom orthotics/prosthetics fabrication is increasingly aided by 3D scanning and printing, but the binding constraint is bespoke hands-on shaping and fitting to an individual body, which no deployed system does end-to-end.

dwa_title: Fabricate medical devices.
rationale: Serial medical device manufacturing is already heavily machine-automated, but custom and low-volume fabrication still requires skilled manual work plus regulated quality sign-off.

dwa_title: Disassemble equipment to inspect for deficiencies.
rationale: Teardown of varied equipment requires dexterous, improvised manipulation and tactile diagnosis; robotic disassembly remains confined to narrow, uniform product lines.

dwa_title: Install production equipment or systems.
rationale: Rigging, aligning and commissioning heavy equipment in an unstructured plant environment is irreducibly embodied; no deployed robot installs other machines.

dwa_title: Install instrumentation or electronic equipment or systems.
rationale: Mounting, wiring and calibrating instrumentation in situ demands fine manual work in confined, non-standard spaces; software can only assist with configuration and documentation.

dwa_title: Adjust prostheses or other assistive devices.
rationale: Fitting depends on tactile adjustment plus real-time patient feedback about comfort, gait and pain — a clinician-patient loop no machine closes.

dwa_title: Adjust dental devices or appliances to ensure fit.
rationale: Digital scanning and CAD/CAM have automated fabrication, but chairside adjustment for occlusion and comfort requires hands in the patient's mouth and licensed responsibility.

dwa_title: Process x-rays or other medical images.
rationale: Image processing is now overwhelmingly digital and pipeline-driven; residual human work is quality checking and handling of physical media or patient positioning.

dwa_title: Create advanced digital images of patients using computer imaging systems.
rationale: Reconstruction and rendering software does the computational work, but acquiring usable images still requires a technologist positioning and reassuring a live patient.

dwa_title: Operate diagnostic or therapeutic medical instruments or equipment.
rationale: Operating instruments on or in a patient carries licensure and direct harm liability; machine control exists only under continuous clinician supervision.

dwa_title: Operate diagnostic imaging equipment.
rationale: Protocol selection and dose optimisation are increasingly automated, but positioning patients and bearing radiation-safety responsibility keeps a credentialed operator in place.

dwa_title: Operate medical equipment.
rationale: Broadly stated clinical equipment operation combines bedside physical presence with regulated accountability for patient safety, which cannot be transferred to a system.

dwa_title: Operate photographic developing or print production equipment.
rationale: Modern digital print and processing lines run largely on automated cycles, but loading media, chemistry handling, color checks and jam clearing still require a body at the machine.

dwa_title: Operate industrial equipment.
rationale: Process control loops automate steady-state running, but setup, changeover, and response to abnormal conditions on industrial plant remain hands-on; the activity is written too broadly for a confident single score.

dwa_title: Operate laboratory or field equipment.
rationale: Bench and field instruments require physical sample handling, calibration and in-situ placement; lab automation covers only high-volume standardized workflows.

dwa_title: Operate precision equipment to control microscopic or nanoscopic processes.
rationale: Nanofabrication and advanced microscopy tools already run scripted, closed-loop recipes, yet alignment, specimen preparation and drift/fault diagnosis keep a skilled operator physically present.

dwa_title: Operate laboratory equipment to analyze medical samples.
rationale: Clinical chemistry and hematology analyzers with track systems already automate the analytic run end-to-end, but specimen integrity checks, instrument QC and the licensure-bound sign-off on results keep a certified technologist in the loop.

dwa_title: Operate farming equipment.
rationale: GPS auto-steer and driverless tractor kits are commercially real but confined to open-field, supervised operations; hitching, implement adjustment and unstructured terrain still demand an operator aboard.

dwa_title: Drive vehicles to transport individuals or equipment.
rationale: Driverless passenger service exists only in narrow geofenced domains with remote support; outside those, legal liability for a vehicle in motion and the physical loading/assisting of people and gear anchor a human driver.

dwa_title: Write computer programming code.
rationale: Code generation is the paradigm case of LLM capability, but specification ambiguity, integration with existing systems and responsibility for shipped defects still bind a human author and reviewer.

dwa_title: Program robotic equipment.
rationale: Path and logic generation can be drafted or synthesized offline, but teaching points, fixturing tolerances and safety validation of a moving machine require on-site commissioning by an accountable engineer.

dwa_title: Implement security measures for computer or information systems.
rationale: Policy-as-code, automated patching and managed detection handle much of the mechanics, but risk trade-offs, adversarial ambiguity and regulatory attestation require a named security owner.

dwa_title: Create electronic data backup to prevent loss of information.
rationale: Scheduled snapshotting, replication and cloud backup services are mature commodity automation; the residual human role is defining retention policy and verifying restores.

dwa_title: Install computer software.
rationale: Package managers, imaging and MDM/endpoint tooling push software at scale without human touch; exceptions are legacy or physically isolated machines and licensing edge cases.

dwa_title: Install computer hardware.
rationale: Racking, cabling and seating components demands dexterous hands in a specific room; no deployed robot handles heterogeneous hardware installs, so only the planning and documentation slices are automatable.

dwa_title: Configure computer networks.
rationale: Infrastructure-as-code, zero-touch provisioning and SDN controllers already push configurations automatically, but design choices, security posture and change approval still route through a named engineer because a bad push can black out a site.

dwa_title: Resolve computer network problems.
rationale: AIOps tools detect and sometimes self-heal known fault patterns, but novel outages mix ambiguous telemetry with physical-layer causes (cables, optics, power) that require someone on site to confirm and fix.

dwa_title: Troubleshoot issues with computer applications or systems.
rationale: Diagnosis from logs, error strings and user descriptions is squarely in frontier-model range, and AI support agents already close simple tickets; the limit is eliciting accurate information from users and safely executing fixes in live systems.

dwa_title: Resolve computer software problems.
rationale: Patch lookup, config repair and code-level debugging are text-native tasks with strong model performance, but authority to change production software and verify the result keeps a human in the loop.

dwa_title: Operate computers or computerized equipment.
rationale: Extremely heterogeneous: console-based operation is scriptable and largely automated, while operating computerized machinery involves loading, monitoring and intervening physically at the equipment.

dwa_title: Operate computer systems.
rationale: Routine system operation is the classic domain of schedulers, orchestration and RPA; the residual human role is exception handling and authorising privileged actions.

dwa_title: Load digital images onto computers or websites.
rationale: Ingest, tag and publish pipelines with automated metadata and CMS APIs already do this end-to-end; only aesthetic selection or rights checking calls for a person.

dwa_title: Enter codes or other information into computers.
rationale: OCR, document AI and RPA handle structured keying at scale in production today; residual human work is exception queues and ambiguous source documents.

dwa_title: Format digital documents, data, or images.
rationale: Formatting is rule-driven transformation of digital artefacts, well covered by templates, scripts and multimodal models, and mistakes are trivially reversible.

dwa_title: Operate digital imaging equipment.
rationale: Automated exposure and image-processing settings are mature, but positioning the subject or document and physically running the scanner or camera ties the work to a location and a pair of hands.

dwa_title: Enter patient or treatment data into computers.
rationale: Ambient scribes and interface engines already draft and post clinical data, but a licensed clinician must attest to the record because coding and charting errors propagate into care decisions and billing liability.

dwa_title: Update website content.
rationale: Content generation and CMS publishing are already scriptable and LLM-drafted; the binding constraint is editorial approval of what goes public under a brand's name, not the mechanics.

dwa_title: Update computer database information.
rationale: Record updating is the archetypal rules-based transaction already handled by integrations, RPA and workflow automation; residual human work is exception handling and source verification.

dwa_title: Enter information into databases or software programs.
rationale: OCR, document-extraction models and RPA now ingest most structured and semi-structured sources end-to-end; only messy or unverifiable source documents still require a keying human.

dwa_title: Prepare data for analysis.
rationale: Cleaning, joining and reshaping data is highly code-generatable, but decisions about outliers, missingness and what counts as valid still shape downstream conclusions and need an analyst's sign-off.

dwa_title: Code data or other information.
rationale: Classification against a codebook (medical, survey, taxonomic) is exactly what current models do well; the constraint is ambiguous edge cases and audit requirements in regulated coding like billing.

dwa_title: Determine design criteria or specifications.
rationale: Setting criteria means reconciling stakeholder needs, cost, regulation and risk tolerance — models can draft and check against standards, but the trade-off choices are owned by a responsible engineer or designer.

dwa_title: Develop specifications for new products or processes.
rationale: Novel product specs require committing an organisation to unproven trade-offs and validating against physical and market realities the model cannot test; drafting and consistency checking are heavily assisted.

dwa_title: Develop specifications or procedures for website development or maintenance.
rationale: Web standards, style guides and maintenance procedures are text artifacts LLMs produce well; the constraint is eliciting and arbitrating what the organisation actually wants and enforcing it.

dwa_title: Develop technical specifications for systems or equipment.
rationale: Equipment and system specs often carry engineering-liability weight and must be reconciled with site conditions and codes, so a licensed engineer signs even when the document is machine-drafted.

dwa_title: Develop specifications for computer network operation.
rationale: Network design specification is well-covered by documented patterns and vendor tooling that models reproduce fluently, but capacity, security and continuity risk keep an accountable architect in the loop.

dwa_title: Determine operational criteria or specifications.
rationale: Operational criteria encode an organisation's risk appetite and resource constraints, information that is tacit and negotiated rather than retrievable, though models can benchmark and draft the resulting standards.

dwa_title: Develop performance metrics or standards related to information technology.
rationale: Drafting SLAs, KPIs and IT standards is document work models handle well, but choosing targets that people will be measured against requires negotiation and managerial ownership.

dwa_title: Plan facility layouts or designs.
rationale: Space-planning and adjacency optimisation are well served by generative layout tools, but reconciling workflow, code, client preference and site idiosyncrasy still requires a human owner of the final plan.

dwa_title: Incorporate green features into the design of structures or facilities.
rationale: Sustainability rating systems and energy-modelling knowledge are highly codified text and calculation, so models can propose measures; the binding constraint is trading off cost, client priorities and certification strategy in a specific project context.

dwa_title: Design civil structures or systems.
rationale: Analysis and code-checking are increasingly software-driven, but civil and structural designs must be sealed by a licensed engineer who bears legal liability for public safety.

dwa_title: Design structures or facilities.
rationale: Parametric and generative design tools produce viable options quickly, yet the binding constraints are client negotiation, site-specific constraints and permit-stage sign-off by a licensed professional.

dwa_title: Design industrial processing systems.
rationale: Process simulation and flowsheet software carries much of the computation, but selecting unit operations under uncertain feedstock, safety and economic assumptions remains an engineer's call with hazard liability attached.

dwa_title: Design industrial equipment.
rationale: CAD plus topology/generative optimisation automates sizing and detailing of components, but integrating manufacturability, maintenance access and plant-floor realities requires a responsible designer.

dwa_title: Design energy production or management equipment or systems.
rationale: Load modelling and equipment selection are computationally tractable, yet grid/utility interconnection standards and high-consequence failure modes keep a licensed engineer accountable for the design.

dwa_title: Design tools, fixtures, or other devices for production equipment.
rationale: Fixture and tooling design is the most rule-bound and library-driven of design tasks, with automated jig generation already in CAM suites; residual work is fitting the tool to an actual machine and part behaviour observed on the floor.

dwa_title: Design control systems for mechanical or other equipment.
rationale: Control logic is symbolic and code-like, which models handle well, but functional-safety certification and the physical consequences of a mis-tuned loop demand human verification and sign-off.

dwa_title: Create models of engineering designs or methods.
rationale: Building CAD/FEA models and scripting simulations is increasingly tool-assisted; the constraint is choosing abstractions and boundary conditions that make the model valid, which is a judgment call.

dwa_title: Develop models of information or communications systems.
rationale: Wholly digital, documentation-like work over formal notations where frontier models are strong; what stops full automation is eliciting real requirements and validating the model against messy existing infrastructure.

dwa_title: Create physical models or prototypes.
rationale: Additive manufacturing and CNC already turn digital models into parts unattended, but fixturing, finishing, assembly and hands-on evaluation of the prototype require bodily presence in the shop.

dwa_title: Design electromechanical equipment or systems.
rationale: EDA and generative CAD tools accelerate topology and component selection, but integrating mechanical motion, thermal and safety constraints requires physical prototyping and a licensed engineer's sign-off on the final design.

dwa_title: Design electrical equipment or systems.
rationale: Code-compliance calculations and schematic generation are increasingly tool-assisted, but electrical designs carry fire and shock liability that statutorily requires a stamped, accountable engineer.

dwa_title: Design electronic or computer equipment or instrumentation.
rationale: Circuit synthesis, place-and-route and firmware scaffolding are already heavily automated in EDA flows, yet architectural trade-offs, novel requirements and silicon validation still anchor a human designer.

dwa_title: Develop procedures for data management.
rationale: Drafting data governance, retention and access procedures is largely document generation an LLM handles well, but the procedures must bind to a specific organizational and regulatory context and be owned by a data steward.

dwa_title: Develop data analysis or data management procedures.
rationale: Analytic pipeline and methodology design is textual and code-like, squarely in LLM range, though validity of the analytic choices against messy real data still needs expert verification.

dwa_title: Develop technical processes to improve the efficiency of biofuel production.
rationale: Process-efficiency gains in biofuel depend on wet-lab experimentation and pilot-plant iteration with living systems; models can propose hypotheses but cannot close the empirical loop.

dwa_title: Develop new or advanced products or production methods.
rationale: Genuine novelty requires physical prototyping, market judgment and iterative experimentation; ideation support is real but the development cycle itself is not automatable end-to-end.

dwa_title: Develop procedures to evaluate organizational activities.
rationale: Evaluation frameworks and metrics can be drafted by a model, but choosing what counts as organizational success is politically negotiated and must be owned by management.

dwa_title: Develop technical methods or processes.
rationale: Broadly worded technical method development typically bottoms out in physical trial and validation in a specific plant or lab, which no deployed system performs autonomously.

dwa_title: Develop testing routines or procedures.
rationale: Test-case generation from specifications is one of the strongest current LLM applications, but coverage adequacy for safety-relevant systems and physical test rig setup keep a human owner.

dwa_title: Develop procedures for data entry or processing.
rationale: Data entry and processing workflows are rule-bound and highly documentable, so drafting them is well within model capability; constraints are mostly integration with legacy systems rather than reasoning.

dwa_title: Establish standards for products, processes, or procedures.
rationale: Standard-setting is an authoritative act: someone with institutional or regulatory standing must adjudicate competing stakeholder interests and be answerable for the threshold chosen, however well a model drafts the text.

dwa_title: Develop agricultural methods.
rationale: Method development rests on empirical field trials in specific soils, climates and crops; models can synthesize agronomic literature and design protocols but cannot generate the site-specific evidence that validates a method.

dwa_title: Establish nursing policies or standards.
rationale: Drafting and harmonizing policy text against regulation and evidence is highly language-shaped, but adoption requires negotiation with clinical staff and a licensed nursing leader who owns the patient-safety consequences.

dwa_title: Develop information communication procedures.
rationale: Communication protocols are essentially documentation work that models draft well; the constraint is fitting them to an organization's actual channels, culture and compliance context, which requires internal knowledge and sign-off.

dwa_title: Establish standards for medical care.
rationale: Care standards carry medico-legal force and must be promulgated by credentialed clinicians answerable for patient harm, even though evidence synthesis and drafting are strongly LLM-exposed.

dwa_title: Develop guidelines for system implementation.
rationale: Implementation guidance is structured technical writing over known architectures, which models handle well; the binding limit is unwritten knowledge of the target environment and stakeholder buy-in.

dwa_title: Develop computer or information security policies or procedures.
rationale: Mapping controls to frameworks and drafting policy language is near-ideal LLM work, but an accountable officer must ratify risk acceptance and attest to compliance for audit and liability purposes.

dwa_title: Maintain facilities.
rationale: Heterogeneous hands-on work across unstructured building environments; no deployed robotics handles the variety of tools, access and improvisation involved.

dwa_title: Repair structural components.
rationale: Structural repair demands in-situ dexterous work on damaged, non-standard geometry, with load-bearing safety consequences that require a competent person on site.

dwa_title: Repair precision devices or workpieces.
rationale: Fine-tolerance diagnosis and manipulation of one-off damaged parts exceeds the fixturing and tactile control of deployed robotic systems.

dwa_title: Replace worn equipment components.
rationale: Predictive analytics can say what to replace, but disassembly and refitting of worn parts in confined, variable machinery remains manual outside a few automated tool-change cells.

dwa_title: Maintain medical equipment or instruments.
rationale: Hands-on cleaning, sterilization, calibration and verification of clinical devices, with regulated documentation that a named technician must certify for patient safety.

dwa_title: Maintain medical laboratory equipment.
rationale: Modern analyzers self-calibrate and flag faults, but physical servicing, reagent handling and QC verification still require a technologist present and accountable under lab accreditation rules.

dwa_title: Repair medical or dental assistive devices.
rationale: Binding constraint is dexterous, highly varied hands-on work on bespoke devices (prosthetics, hearing aids, dental appliances) often fitted to an individual patient; only diagnostic reasoning and documentation are model-exposed.

dwa_title: Repair medical facility equipment.
rationale: Repair of imaging, monitoring and life-support equipment requires in-situ physical service plus regulated sign-off that a named biomedical technician must provide; AI can only assist fault isolation.

dwa_title: Maintain mechanical equipment.
rationale: Lubrication, adjustment and part replacement demand hands on machinery in unstructured settings; sensor-based condition monitoring automates the detection half but not the intervention.

dwa_title: Maintain work equipment or machinery.
rationale: Generic hands-on upkeep of heterogeneous machinery; the physical variability of access, fasteners and wear defeats today's robotics even where scheduling and logging are automated.

dwa_title: Maintain electromechanical equipment.
rationale: Electromechanical servicing couples electrical fault tracing, which models can guide, with physical disassembly and alignment that must be done on site.

dwa_title: Maintain equipment or systems to ensure proper functioning.
rationale: Written broadly enough to include automated monitoring and self-healing systems, but the corrective action still typically requires a technician physically present.

dwa_title: Repair electronic equipment.
rationale: Board-level fault tracing, soldering and component replacement need fine manipulation and test instruments in hand; the constraint is embodiment, not diagnostic reasoning.

dwa_title: Maintain computer hardware.
rationale: Firmware updates and remote diagnostics are automatable, but swapping drives, cards and cables and racking hardware still requires a person at the machine.

dwa_title: Maintain computer networks to enhance performance and user access.
rationale: Configuration, monitoring, tuning and troubleshooting are software-mediated and highly model-exposed, but change control on production networks keeps a human owning the risk, plus residual cabling work.

dwa_title: Maintain electronic equipment.
rationale: Routine cleaning, testing, calibration and part replacement of electronic gear are physical tasks in situ; AI contributes fault interpretation and record-keeping only.

dwa_title: Maintain laboratory or technical equipment.
rationale: Calibration and servicing of instruments must be performed and certified on the bench; accreditation regimes require a named technician's calibration record even where data analysis is automated.

dwa_title: Maintain computer equipment or software.
rationale: The software half (patching, imaging, configuration management) is already heavily scripted and model-assistable, while the equipment half still needs physical hands, so neither side dominates.

dwa_title: Maintain test equipment.
rationale: Calibration, cleaning, part replacement and functional checks on physical instruments demand dexterous hands-on work in situ; software can schedule and log maintenance but cannot perform it.

dwa_title: Prepare financial documents, reports, or budgets.
rationale: Ledger systems and LLMs can assemble and draft most statements and budget schedules, but attestation, assumption-setting and regulatory sign-off require a named accountable preparer.

dwa_title: Present research results to others.
rationale: Slide and narrative generation is highly exposed, but the act of presenting—fielding challenges, defending methods to a live audience—is a relational performance attributed to a specific researcher.

dwa_title: Present medical research reports.
rationale: Clinical findings presented to peers or regulators carry authorship liability and require live defense of methodology; drafting support is strong but the speaker must own the claims.

dwa_title: Prepare research or technical reports.
rationale: Structuring, drafting and summarising results is squarely in frontier-model territory; the binding constraint is verified fidelity to underlying data and a human author accepting responsibility for conclusions.

dwa_title: Prepare scientific or technical reports or presentations.
rationale: Text and slide production from data is largely model-doable; hallucination risk and authorship accountability keep a scientist in the loop for verification.

dwa_title: Prepare analytical reports.
rationale: Analysis-to-narrative is the paradigm LLM task and templated analytics pipelines already auto-generate reports; interpretation choices and data validation still need human sign-off.

dwa_title: Write reports or evaluations.
rationale: Drafting is heavily exposed, but 'evaluations' often carry consequences for people or programs, so the evaluative judgment and its attribution must remain with a named human.

dwa_title: Prepare research or technical reports on environmental issues.
rationale: Environmental impact and compliance documents follow templates an LLM handles well, but they are regulatory filings typically requiring a licensed professional's certification of field data and conclusions.

dwa_title: Prepare technical or operational reports.
rationale: Operational reporting is often already auto-generated from instrumented systems; residual human role is anomaly interpretation and attesting to accuracy.

dwa_title: Prepare technical reports for internal use.
rationale: Internal-audience technical write-ups have low external liability and abundant structured source data, so model drafting plus light review can carry most of the task.

dwa_title: Record images needed to address work issues.
rationale: Someone or something must be physically at the scene with a camera and choose what evidence to capture; fixed cameras and drones automate only pre-arranged viewpoints.

dwa_title: Document events or evidence, using photographic or audiovisual equipment.
