rationale: Capturing evidence requires a camera physically present at the scene with framing choices made in situ; fixed automated cameras cover only a narrow slice, and chain-of-custody integrity demands a named human.

dwa_title: Prepare official health documents or records.
rationale: Generation of official health records is textual and highly LLM-exposed, but statutory and licensure rules require a credentialed human to attest to the contents.

dwa_title: Prepare reports summarizing patient diagnostic or care activities.
rationale: Summarising diagnostic and care data is exactly what clinical-note LLM tools already do well; the binding constraint is clinician sign-off and liability for diagnostic content.

dwa_title: Develop proposals for current or prospective customers.
rationale: Drafting is near-fully LLM-exposed, but pricing, commitments and reading the customer's unstated priorities require a human owning the client relationship.

dwa_title: Write grant proposals.
rationale: Grant text is prime LLM territory, yet the substantive scientific/programmatic claims and the institutional signature behind them must come from a responsible human.

dwa_title: Prepare proposal documents.
rationale: Document assembly from templates and prior content is largely automatable; the binding constraint is that the substantive offer and its accuracy still need human commitment.

dwa_title: Prepare proposals or grant applications to obtain project funding.
rationale: Writing and compliance-checking funding applications is text-heavy and well served by models, but budget commitments and certification of accuracy rest on a named applicant.

dwa_title: Prepare proposal documents or grant applications.
rationale: Essentially a drafting-and-assembly task that current models handle at speed; human ownership persists for substantive claims and signature authority.

dwa_title: Document operational activities.
rationale: Operational logging is increasingly captured automatically by instrumented systems; residual human input is needed only where events are observed off-system.

dwa_title: Maintain student records.
rationale: Student information systems already handle entry, updates and reporting by rule; the remaining constraint is privacy/records-custodian accountability rather than capability.

dwa_title: Maintain records of customer accounts.
rationale: CRM and billing platforms maintain account records automatically from transactions; exceptions and disputes are the only part needing human handling.

dwa_title: Record research or operational data.
rationale: Digital instrumentation and data-capture systems record most research and operational data without human transcription; manual recording persists where readings or observations are made by hand at the bench or site.

dwa_title: Document operational procedures.
rationale: Writing up how a process works is near-pure text generation that LLMs handle well, but the tacit, undocumented knowledge of the actual procedure has to be elicited from practitioners and validated before it becomes an authoritative document.

dwa_title: Maintain operational records or records systems.
rationale: Modern ERP, MES and logging systems already capture and organize operational records automatically; the binding constraint is data entry at points where events are not yet instrumented and exception handling when entries conflict.

dwa_title: Maintain repair or maintenance records.
rationale: CMMS platforms automate most of the record structure, but maintenance logs in regulated domains (aviation, medical devices, lifts) legally require a named certifying technician's attestation that the work was actually performed.

dwa_title: Maintain operational records.
rationale: Where operations are already digitally instrumented, record maintenance is a solved software problem; the residual human work is capturing events that never touch a system.

dwa_title: Record agricultural or forestry inventory data.
rationale: The recording step is trivially digital, but generating the inventory figures for crops, livestock or timber still depends on in-field observation, counting and measurement; remote sensing covers only part of it.

dwa_title: Maintain records, documents, or other files.
rationale: Document management systems with automated classification and retention rules already handle this; physical paper files and scanning are the remaining manual residue.

dwa_title: Prepare procedural documents.
rationale: Drafting SOPs and manuals is squarely in an LLM's wheelhouse, but the content must be sourced from subject-matter experts and formally approved, since people will follow the procedure as written.

dwa_title: Document technical design details.
rationale: Design documentation can be largely generated from CAD models, code and change logs, but accurately capturing design intent and rationale still requires the designer's own account.

dwa_title: Document network-related activities or tasks.
rationale: Network discovery, configuration management and ticketing tools already auto-generate topology maps and activity logs, and LLMs write the narrative layer over them.

dwa_title: Document technical specifications or requirements.
rationale: Specification writing is text-heavy and heavily LLM-assisted, but requirements must be elicited and negotiated among stakeholders and then owned contractually by a responsible engineer.

dwa_title: Document design or development procedures.
rationale: Much of this can be synthesized from version control, issue trackers and design artifacts, but completeness and fidelity to what was actually done require human verification.

dwa_title: Document test results.
rationale: Automated test harnesses and LIMS already capture and report results without human transcription; the constraint is regulated contexts (clinical, aerospace, certified labs) where a qualified individual must sign off on the record's validity.

dwa_title: Document design or operational test results.
rationale: Test benches and instrumentation already auto-log data, and language models can draft the narrative and interpretation, but the binding constraint is authenticated engineering sign-off on what the results mean for a design's fitness.

dwa_title: Maintain records of sales or other business transactions.
rationale: POS, ERP and accounting platforms already capture and post transactions without human transcription; only exception handling and reconciliation of anomalies still pull a person in.

dwa_title: Maintain medical facility records.
rationale: EHR and health-information-management systems automate storage, indexing and coding suggestions, but privacy law and release-of-information rules require a named custodian answerable for record integrity.

dwa_title: Record vital statistics or other health information.
rationale: Device-to-record interfaces already push vitals automatically, but obtaining the measurement at the bedside and attesting to statutory registry accuracy keeps a licensed human in the chain.

dwa_title: Record patient medical histories.
rationale: Ambient AI scribes now draft histories from clinical conversation at scale, but the clinician must elicit and verify the content because an erroneous history propagates into diagnosis and liability.

dwa_title: Maintain medical records.
rationale: Most maintenance operations are database transactions machines handle well; the constraint is regulated accountability for completeness, amendment and disclosure of the legal medical record.

dwa_title: Develop training materials.
rationale: Generative models produce usable curricula, slides and assessments directly, so the remaining human role is needs analysis, organisational context and validating that the material actually changes behaviour.

dwa_title: Create technology-based learning materials.
rationale: Authoring tools plus generative text, image and voice cover most content production, but integration into an LMS, accessibility compliance and interaction design still require human assembly.

dwa_title: Prepare healthcare training materials.
rationale: Drafting is squarely in model capability, but clinical accuracy and accreditation of healthcare instruction demand review by a credentialed subject-matter expert who bears responsibility for errors taught to practitioners.

dwa_title: Prepare informational or reference materials.
rationale: This is essentially synthesis and exposition of existing information, which deployed language models perform end-to-end; only factual verification and house-style approval remain human.

dwa_title: Prepare instruction manuals.
rationale: Models draft procedures well from specifications, but hands-on validation that the documented steps actually work, plus liability for safety warnings, anchors a human reviewer.

dwa_title: Develop instructional materials.
rationale: Content generation and alignment to stated learning objectives are automatable; the constraint is contested pedagogical judgment about sequencing and fit to a particular learner population.

dwa_title: Prepare sales or other contracts.
rationale: Template-and-clause assembly is already largely software-driven and LLMs draft terms well, but the binding constraint is that a named party or licensed agent must own the enforceable commitments and negotiated deviations.

dwa_title: Prepare documentation for permits or licenses.
rationale: Permit and licence packages are highly structured and form-driven, so extraction and population are automatable; the constraint is jurisdiction-specific evidentiary requirements and the signed attestation of accuracy demanded by the issuing authority.

dwa_title: Prepare contracts, disclosures, or applications.
rationale: Drafting contracts, disclosures and applications is text generation over structured facts, which frontier models handle; disclosure obligations carry legal liability that requires a responsible human signatory.

dwa_title: Maintain regulatory or compliance documentation.
rationale: Document control, versioning and retention are classic workflow-automation targets, but deciding what satisfies an inspector or auditor and certifying the record remains a named compliance officer's duty.

dwa_title: Prepare information or documentation related to legal or regulatory matters.
rationale: Legal and regulatory drafting is the paradigm case of high LLM leverage, yet unauthorised-practice rules, filing certifications and liability for misstatement anchor responsibility to a licensed human.

dwa_title: Prepare reports detailing student activities or performance.
rationale: Grade and attendance data already auto-populate report cards, but the qualitative narrative rests on a teacher's direct observation of a child and is read by parents as a professional judgment.

dwa_title: Prepare accident or incident reports.
rationale: The binding constraint is firsthand observation and witness interviewing at the scene plus the report's use as a legal and insurance record requiring an attesting human author.

dwa_title: Prepare operational reports.
rationale: Operational reporting draws on instrumented system data, and BI pipelines plus generated narrative summaries already produce these routinely with minimal review.

dwa_title: Prepare operational progress or status reports.
rationale: Status and progress reporting is mostly aggregation of tracked metrics into prose, a task deployed dashboards and LLM summarisers perform end-to-end; only contested interpretations of slippage need a human.

dwa_title: Write articles, books or other original materials in area of expertise.
rationale: Models generate fluent long-form prose but genuine originality, subject-matter authority and reputational authorship are the value being sold, so the expert's name and vetting remain load-bearing.

dwa_title: Explain engineering drawings, specifications, or other technical information.
rationale: Multimodal reading of drawings is still unreliable for dimensioned engineering documents, and the work is a live dialogue calibrated to what a specific tradesperson or client misunderstands, with build errors as the downside.

dwa_title: Explain technical product or service information to customers.
rationale: Retrieval-grounded assistants are already commercially deployed for exactly this explaining-to-customers function; the residual human need is escalation for frustrated customers and high-stakes specification claims.

dwa_title: Inform the public about policies, services or procedures.
rationale: Public information delivery is largely text/voice generation over a known policy corpus, which chatbots already do at scale; the binding constraint is institutional liability for misinformation and the need for a named spokesperson in contested cases.

dwa_title: Explain regulations, policies, or procedures.
rationale: Interpreting and restating rules in plain language is a core LLM strength, but authoritative interpretation of regulation carries legal consequence that organizations still route through accountable staff.

dwa_title: Communicate organizational information to customers or other stakeholders.
rationale: Routine stakeholder and customer communication is already heavily automated through templated messaging, CRM workflows and conversational agents; only sensitive or relationship-critical disclosures are held back.

dwa_title: Translate information for others.
rationale: Machine translation is a mature deployed technology handling most general-purpose language conversion end-to-end; certified legal, medical and literary translation remains human-signed for fidelity and liability.

dwa_title: Interpret cultural or religious information for others.
rationale: Models hold broad cultural and doctrinal knowledge, but conveying meaning that is contested, community-specific and identity-laden depends on standing and trust the speaker holds within that community.

dwa_title: Explain financial information to customers.
rationale: Explanation of statements, products and terms is readily generated, but financial suitability and disclosure rules bind a licensed individual to what the customer is told.

dwa_title: Communicate detailed medical information to patients or family members.
rationale: Content can be drafted and tailored by a model, but informed consent and disclosure of diagnosis legally attach to a licensed clinician who must read and respond to the patient's emotional state in real time.

dwa_title: Confer with family members to discuss client treatment plans or progress.
rationale: The substance is a negotiated, emotionally charged conversation with a family about care decisions; the relationship and the clinician's accountability for the plan are the work itself.

dwa_title: Confer with clients to discuss treatment plans or progress.
rationale: Treatment planning conferences require therapeutic alliance, consent and clinical responsibility; model assistance is confined to preparation and documentation.

dwa_title: Explain medical procedures or test results to patients or family members.
rationale: Portals already release results with automated explanations, yet interpreting significant findings for a patient is a regulated clinical act requiring a named responsible practitioner.

dwa_title: Communicate with the public on environmental issues.
rationale: Material preparation and routine inquiry response are highly model-exposed, but public environmental communication is politically contested and often occurs in hearings and site meetings where a credible human must stand behind claims.

dwa_title: Communicate green energy production information.
rationale: This is largely reporting technical production data and explaining it, well within automated data-to-narrative pipelines; residual constraint is verification of figures that may carry regulatory or investor weight.

dwa_title: Communicate results of environmental research.
rationale: Drafting reports, visualisations and summaries of environmental findings is squarely in LLM territory, but the scientist must vouch for the interpretation and defend it to regulators or the public.

dwa_title: Collaborate on research activities with scientists or technical specialists.
rationale: The substance is sustained peer collaboration — negotiating design choices and dividing labour with colleagues — which a model can support intellectually but cannot be a party to.

dwa_title: Assist engineers or scientists with research.
rationale: Heterogeneous support role: literature and data-analysis components are highly exposed, but much assisting involves bench or field work under a scientist's direction.

dwa_title: Communicate with other workers to coordinate activities.
rationale: Scheduling and dispatch systems automate the routine signalling, but the binding constraint is that coordination is a live negotiation between accountable humans about who does what.

dwa_title: Report information to managers or other personnel.
rationale: Routine status and exception reporting upward is largely a data-aggregation-and-summarise task already handled by dashboards and automated reports.

dwa_title: Confer with organizational members to accomplish work activities.
rationale: Conferring is the relationship itself — mutual commitment among organisational members — so tools can prepare and minute it but not replace the participants.

dwa_title: Confer with coworkers to coordinate work activities.
rationale: Peer-to-peer work coordination depends on reciprocal human commitment and tacit context; software can only schedule and notify around it.

dwa_title: Confer with others to conduct or arrange operational activities.
rationale: Arranging operations has a substantial bookable, rule-based layer that agents can now handle, but the conferring and trade-off negotiation with counterparties stays human.

dwa_title: Provide information to coworkers.
rationale: Answering colleagues' informational questions is retrieval and explanation, which internal knowledge assistants already do at scale.

dwa_title: Exchange information with colleagues.
rationale: Bidirectional exchange presupposes two informed participants with context and stake; automation handles the transmission and summarisation layer only.

dwa_title: Communicate safety or hazard information to others.
rationale: Hazard alerts and toolbox-talk content can be generated automatically, but OSHA-style duties require a named person to have communicated and confirmed comprehension, and failure is life-threatening.

dwa_title: Communicate with others to coordinate vehicle movement.
rationale: Automated ground-movement and traffic-control aids exist, but responsibility for real-time vehicle separation rests with licensed controllers and spotters because errors are immediate and physical.

dwa_title: Liaise between departments or other groups to improve function or communication.
rationale: The substance is brokering trust and surfacing tacit friction between groups, which requires standing in a live relational position; LLMs can draft the memos and summarise cross-team status but cannot hold the boundary-spanning role.

dwa_title: Inform medical professionals regarding patient conditions and care.
rationale: Clinical handoff content is highly summarisable from the record, but a licensed clinician must be answerable for what is conveyed and for the judgment about what matters, so the model can prepare but not own the communication.

dwa_title: Confer with other professionals to plan patient care.
rationale: Care planning is a licensed, negotiated professional act where named clinicians accept liability for the plan; decision support can propose options but the conferral itself is legally lodged in humans.

dwa_title: Collaborate with other professionals to assess client needs or plan treatments.
rationale: Multidisciplinary needs assessment turns on reconciling divergent professional readings of an ambiguous case, and each discipline signs for its own contribution.

dwa_title: Communicate test or assessment results to medical professionals.
rationale: Automated result routing, critical-value alerting and structured report delivery are already deployed; what still binds is a qualified signatory for interpretation and confirmation that urgent findings were actually received.

dwa_title: Collaborate with healthcare professionals to plan or provide treatment.
rationale: The activity bundles joint deliberation with actual treatment delivery, so both licensure accountability and hands-on presence keep it lodged in clinicians.

dwa_title: Collaborate with others to develop or implement marketing strategies.
rationale: Strategy generation, segmentation analysis and campaign drafting are squarely in model territory; the binding constraint is that stakeholder buy-in and internal negotiation over resources happen between people.

dwa_title: Share sales-related or market information with colleagues.
rationale: CRM dashboards, automated pipeline digests and market-intelligence summarisation already push this information to colleagues without human mediation; only nuanced field colour still needs a person.

dwa_title: Collaborate with other agencies and institutions to coordinate educational matters.
rationale: Inter-agency coordination is institutional relationship work with competing mandates and political sensitivities; models can prepare agendas and reconcile documents but not represent the institution.

dwa_title: Report maintenance or equipment problems to appropriate personnel.
rationale: Sensor telemetry, condition monitoring and automated work-order ticketing already detect and route equipment faults end-to-end; the residual human role is noticing problems that instrumentation does not cover.

dwa_title: Confer with technical personnel to prepare designs or operational plans.
rationale: Specification reconciliation, constraint checking and plan drafting are strongly model-exposed, but sign-off on engineered designs rests with responsible professionals and the conferral resolves genuine technical disagreement.

dwa_title: Collaborate with others to develop or refine designs.
rationale: Generative and multimodal tools already iterate design variants quickly; what remains human is the shared taste-and-tradeoff negotiation that converges a team on one refined option.

dwa_title: Discuss design or technical features of products or services with technical personnel.
rationale: Models can generate and critique technical design content fluently, but the activity is a live negotiation of shared understanding among engineers, so the human dialogue partner cannot be removed without removing the task itself.

dwa_title: Collaborate with others to determine design specifications or details.
rationale: Specification trade-offs can be drafted and explored by a model, but reaching agreement across stakeholders with competing priorities is the binding constraint and remains a human bargaining process.

dwa_title: Consult with others regarding safety or health equipment or facilities.
rationale: Regulatory codes and equipment specs are highly retrievable text, but safety consultation carries named liability and often requires site-specific observation, anchoring it to an accountable person.

dwa_title: Communicate project information to others.
rationale: Status summarisation and distribution is already partly automated by project tooling and generative reporting; what resists is tailoring emphasis to audiences and fielding follow-up in real time.

dwa_title: Confer with clients to exchange information.
rationale: Conversational agents already handle routine client information exchange, but eliciting unstated needs and sustaining a trusted commercial relationship keeps a human in the seat for anything non-routine.

dwa_title: Discuss designs or plans with clients.
rationale: Generative tools can visualise and explain plan options instantly, yet interpreting a client's vague aesthetic or functional preferences and winning their sign-off is relational work.

dwa_title: Testify at legal or legislative proceedings.
rationale: Testimony is sworn by a named individual subject to perjury and cross-examination; no machine can hold that legal standing regardless of how well it could prepare the content.

dwa_title: Represent the interests of clients in legal proceedings.
rationale: Appearance before a tribunal requires a licensed advocate with fiduciary duty; unauthorised-practice rules and courtroom standing are the binding constraint, not drafting ability.

dwa_title: Communicate health and wellness information to the public.
rationale: Health messaging is text and media production that models do well, but public health claims require an accountable clinician or agency to vouch for accuracy given the harm from misinformation.

dwa_title: Inform viewers, listeners, or audiences.
rationale: Automated scripting, voice synthesis and synthetic presenters already deliver informational broadcasts, but editorial responsibility and audience trust in a recognisable human still gate full substitution.

dwa_title: Present sustainable products or services information to the public.
rationale: This is essentially content generation and explanation, highly exposed to models; the constraint is that sustainability claims invite greenwashing liability and so need a human endorser.

dwa_title: Present information to the public.
rationale: Written and recorded public communication is already routinely machine-drafted, but live presentation and responsiveness to an audience still favour a human deliverer; the activity is too generic to score tightly.

dwa_title: Provide educational information to the public.
rationale: The content is pure information transfer that models handle well, but public education often happens in live settings where reading an audience and adapting delivery still binds it to a person.

dwa_title: Provide technical information or assistance to public.
rationale: Technical Q&A is squarely in LLM territory and already deployed as support assistants; the constraint is that technical advice to outsiders can carry liability and often needs site- or case-specific verification.

dwa_title: Explain project details to the general public.
rationale: Drafting the explanation is easy for a model, but the activity typically means facing skeptical stakeholders at public meetings, where credibility and live handling of objections are the actual work.

dwa_title: Provide information to the general public.
rationale: Generic public information delivery is already displaced at scale by websites, chatbots and voice agents; only edge cases and vulnerable callers escalate to humans.

dwa_title: Answer telephones to direct calls or provide information.
rationale: Call routing and canned information delivery is the most thoroughly automated communication task in existence, with IVR and now conversational voice agents commercially deployed end-to-end.

dwa_title: Provide customer service to clients or users.
rationale: Tier-one service is being absorbed by deployed AI agents, but emotional escalation, goodwill concessions and exception handling still get handed to a human with authority to act.

dwa_title: Provide customers with general information or assistance.
rationale: General enquiry handling is low-stakes, script-shaped and grounded in retrievable knowledge bases, which is exactly what current deployed assistants do reliably.

dwa_title: Provide basic information to guests, visitors, or clients.
rationale: Kiosks and digital concierges already substitute for much of this, though physical presence at a desk still carries a greeting and reassurance function machines handle poorly.

dwa_title: Develop collaborative relationships between departments or with external organizations.
rationale: Trust between organisations is held by named individuals with reputations and reciprocal obligations; software can schedule and draft but cannot be the party to a relationship.

dwa_title: Establish interpersonal business relationships to facilitate work activities.
rationale: The relationship itself is the deliverable, and counterparties extend goodwill to a person rather than to a system, so delegation destroys the value created.

dwa_title: Refer customers to appropriate personnel.
rationale: Matching a stated need to the right internal party is a classification and routing problem already handled by deployed triage and ticketing systems.

dwa_title: Refer patients to other healthcare practitioners or health resources.
rationale: A referral is a clinical decision that a licensed practitioner must sign and answer for; delayed or misdirected referrals cause real harm regardless of how well a model can suggest options.

dwa_title: Treat patients using psychological therapies.
rationale: The therapeutic alliance itself is the active ingredient, and licensure plus suicide/harm risk require a named clinician; chatbots can deliver manualised CBT content but cannot own the case.

dwa_title: Implement therapeutic programs to improve patient functioning.
rationale: Program design and progress tracking are highly model-exposed, but implementation means in-person coaching, motivating and adapting to a patient in real time.

dwa_title: Treat patients using physical therapy techniques.
rationale: Manual therapy, palpation and hands-on guarding of an unstable patient require dexterous physical presence no deployed robot provides; licensed accountability compounds this.

dwa_title: Administer medical substances for imaging or other procedures.
rationale: Power injectors automate the bolus, but venous access, contrast-reaction vigilance and radiopharmaceutical handling need a licensed human at the bedside.

dwa_title: Apply bandages, dressings, or splints.
rationale: Wrapping and immobilising a variably shaped, painful human limb is a fine-motor compliant-manipulation task far outside deployed robotics.

dwa_title: Administer basic health care or medical treatments.
rationale: Hands-on contact with a patient's body plus scope-of-practice licensure make this irreducibly human, even where decision support is strong.

dwa_title: Administer anesthetics or sedatives to control pain.
rationale: Closed-loop sedation systems exist but were largely withdrawn; airway rescue and the legal requirement for an accountable anesthesia provider bind absolutely.

dwa_title: Care for women during pregnancy and childbirth.
rationale: Intrapartum care is simultaneously manual, emotionally intensive and catastrophically consequential; monitoring algorithms only inform the attending clinician.

dwa_title: Provide basic health care services.
rationale: Broad bedside care bundles physical assistance with reassurance and triage judgment; automation reaches only the documentation and guidance layer.

dwa_title: Administer non-intravenous medications.
rationale: Pharmacy robots and dispensing cabinets automate preparation, but placing oral or topical medication into a specific patient and verifying ingestion remains a hands-on, signed-for act.

dwa_title: Immunize patients.
rationale: Injection into a moving human plus anaphylaxis readiness and vaccination-record liability keep a licensed injector in place despite the task's protocol-driven simplicity.

dwa_title: Administer intravenous medications.
rationale: Smart pumps automate infusion rates, but cannulation, line verification and the high-severity consequences of a wrong IV drug demand an accountable clinician's hands.

dwa_title: Administer blood or other fluids intravenously.
rationale: Venipuncture and IV therapy require fine dexterous manipulation on a living body plus licensed clinical accountability; infusion pumps automate delivery rate but not cannulation or monitoring judgment.

dwa_title: Care for plants or animals.
rationale: Irrigation, climate control and automated feeders cover routine slices, but unstructured handling of living organisms in varied environments still needs hands and eyes on site.

dwa_title: Care for animals.
rationale: Animals are unpredictable moving subjects requiring tactile handling and behavioural reading; only feeding, watering and environmental monitoring are reliably mechanised.

dwa_title: Perform animal breeding procedures.
rationale: Estrus detection sensors and genetic-matching software are widely deployed, but insemination and obstetric handling remain manual procedures on live animals.

dwa_title: Provide care for animals.
rationale: Same binding constraint as general animal care: physical presence and dexterous, responsive handling of a living creature that cannot be standardised.

dwa_title: Respond to emergencies to provide assistance.
rationale: Emergency response demands bodily presence in chaotic, unmodelled scenes plus legal responsibility for life-safety decisions; AI can only assist with dispatch triage and information.

dwa_title: Fit eyeglasses, contact lenses, or other vision aids.
rationale: Automated refraction and lens-ordering software handle the measurement and specification, but physical fitting, adjustment and comfort verification on a person's face or eye require hands and licensed sign-off.

dwa_title: Provide first aid or rescue assistance in emergencies.
rationale: Hands-on stabilisation and extraction of an injured person in an unstructured environment has no deployed robotic substitute; only coached instruction over phone is automatable.

dwa_title: Treat medical emergencies.
rationale: Time-critical diagnosis and intervention on an unstable patient carries licensure liability and irreversible consequences; decision support can inform but never own the act.

dwa_title: Implement advanced life support techniques.
rationale: Protocol-driven enough that AEDs and mechanical CPR devices exist, yet intubation, drug administration and code leadership require a credentialed clinician physically at the bedside.

dwa_title: Assist patients with hygiene or daily living activities.
rationale: Intimate bodily assistance combines dexterous contact with a vulnerable person and a dignity-laden relationship that no deployed machine can substitute for.

dwa_title: Assist clients in handling details of daily life.
rationale: Scheduling, form-filling and benefits navigation are highly LLM-exposed, but the work is anchored in a trusted ongoing relationship with a dependent person and frequent errands in the physical world.

dwa_title: Assist students with special educational needs.
rationale: The binding constraint is the relational and often physical nature of supporting a child with disabilities in situ; adaptive software can supplement instruction but cannot hold the duty of care or read a distressed student's behaviour in real time.

dwa_title: Assist patients with daily activities.
rationale: Bathing, toileting, feeding and transferring a frail human body requires dexterous, gentle contact that no deployed robot can perform; assistive lifts only reduce the human's load.

dwa_title: Assist customers to ensure comfort or safety.
rationale: Kiosks and chat agents handle the informational slice, but attending to a patron's physical comfort and safety on site requires a present body able to intervene.

dwa_title: Position patients for treatment or examination.
rationale: Motorised tables and auto-positioning imaging systems assist, but manually arranging a compliant or injured patient's limbs and torso demands hands-on contact and reassurance.

dwa_title: Assist healthcare practitioners during examinations or treatments.
rationale: Anticipating a clinician's next need and handing instruments or steadying a patient is tacit, fast-paced physical teamwork far beyond deployed robotics.

dwa_title: Assist healthcare practitioners during surgery.
rationale: Intraoperative assisting combines sterile manual dexterity with licensed accountability inside the operating team; surgical robots are teleoperated, not autonomous assistants.

dwa_title: Prepare patients physically for medical procedures.
rationale: Shaving, draping, prepping skin and verifying site require touch on the patient plus a named clinician answerable for pre-procedure safety checks.

dwa_title: Maintain sterile operative fields.
rationale: Sterility is maintained by continuous embodied vigilance over a physical field; contamination is invisible to sensors in practice and a licensed scrub person must attest to it.

dwa_title: Care for patients with mental illnesses.
rationale: Therapeutic alliance, crisis de-escalation and risk-of-harm decisions are inherently relational and legally assigned to licensed clinicians, even though LLMs can support documentation and psychoeducation.

dwa_title: Treat acute illnesses, infections, or injuries.
rationale: Diagnostic reasoning is highly LLM-exposed, but examination, procedures and prescribing authority require a licensed practitioner physically present and legally answerable.

dwa_title: Operate on patients to treat conditions.
rationale: Operating is irreversible manipulation of living tissue under surprise conditions; existing robots amplify a surgeon's hands rather than replacing the responsible operator.

dwa_title: Treat dental problems or diseases.
rationale: Intraoral work needs fine instrument control in a confined, wet, moving field; CAD/CAM and robotic implant guidance automate only planning and drilling paths under dentist supervision.

dwa_title: Treat animal injuries or illnesses.
rationale: Hands-on physical intervention on a non-verbal patient plus veterinary licensure means only diagnostic reasoning support is automatable.

dwa_title: Administer cancer treatments.
rationale: Chemotherapy and radiation delivery are partially machine-executed but dose planning, consent and toxicity management require a licensed clinician who is legally answerable for a life-threatening error margin.

dwa_title: Treat chronic diseases or disorders.
rationale: Chronic disease management is heavily information-based and algorithm-assisted, but prescribing authority, longitudinal patient relationship and adherence coaching keep a licensed human accountable.

dwa_title: Treat patients using alternative medical procedures.
rationale: Acupuncture, manipulation and similar modalities are inherently manual and their therapeutic effect is bound up with the practitioner-patient encounter.

dwa_title: Advocate for individual or community needs.
rationale: Drafting arguments and briefs is highly LLM-exposed, but advocacy derives its force from a legitimate human speaking on someone's behalf before other humans.

dwa_title: Merchandise healthcare products or services.
rationale: Content generation, targeting and product positioning are automatable, but regulated healthcare claims and clinician relationships require human oversight and presence.

dwa_title: Sell products or services.
rationale: E-commerce and recommendation engines already close simple transactions end-to-end, but consultative and high-value selling still turns on trust built between people.

dwa_title: Customize energy products or services to meet customer needs.
rationale: Configuring energy plans is data-driven analysis that models handle well; the constraint is contract negotiation and regulated disclosures with a customer.

dwa_title: Perform marketing activities.
rationale: Copy, segmentation, campaign optimisation and analytics are already substantially machine-run; strategic positioning and brand accountability keep humans in the loop.

dwa_title: Promote products, services, or programs.
rationale: Promotional content production and distribution are highly LLM-exposed; the residual human work is relationship-based outreach and reputational risk ownership.

dwa_title: Demonstrate products to consumers.
rationale: Live product demonstration requires physically handling the item in front of an audience and reading their reactions; video substitutes exist but do not replace in-person demos.

dwa_title: Promote environmental sustainability or conservation initiatives.
rationale: Educational materials and messaging generate easily, but changing behaviour and mobilising communities depends on credible human messengers and local presence.

dwa_title: Market products, services, or events.
rationale: Content generation, targeting and campaign optimisation are already machine-run in ad platforms, but positioning strategy, brand risk and channel choice still hinge on human market judgement and sign-off.

dwa_title: Contact current or potential customers to promote products or services.
rationale: Automated email/SMS sequences and increasingly voice agents already handle high-volume outreach; the binding constraint is customer tolerance and the relationship-building that converts contact into commitment for anything beyond commodity sales.

dwa_title: Promote educational institutions or programs.
rationale: Recruitment materials and inquiry handling are highly automatable, but enrolment persuasion involves counselling prospective students and families in person, plus regulated accuracy in representing programmes.

dwa_title: Deliver promotional presentations to current or prospective customers.
rationale: Preparing the deck is near-fully automatable, but live delivery requires reading a room and responding to objections in real time, which buyers still expect from a human representative.

dwa_title: Distribute promotional literature or samples to customers.
rationale: Mail and fulfilment channels are automated, but handing samples or flyers to people in a store, event or street setting requires physical presence and dexterity no deployed system provides.

dwa_title: Mediate disputes.
rationale: Neutrality, trust and the capacity to manage emotion between adversaries are the substance of mediation, and legal or professional frameworks require an identifiable, accountable neutral.

dwa_title: Negotiate sales or lease agreements for products or services.
rationale: Models can price, draft and simulate concessions, but binding a counterparty to terms requires authority to commit the organisation and a signatory who bears the legal consequences.

dwa_title: Negotiate contracts with clients or service providers.
rationale: Clause analysis and counter-offer generation are strong AI territory, and autonomous procurement negotiation bots exist for tail spend, but strategic client relationships and contractual liability keep a named human in charge.

dwa_title: Negotiate project specifications.
rationale: Trading off scope, cost and technical feasibility across stakeholders with conflicting priorities is contested judgement that must be owned by someone answerable for delivery.

dwa_title: Negotiate contracts for transportation, distribution, or logistics services.
rationale: Freight rate negotiation is the most algorithmically advanced case, with digital marketplaces and automated bidding already closing spot deals, yet contractual commitment and carrier relationships remain human-held.

dwa_title: Negotiate prices or other sales terms.
rationale: Dynamic pricing engines and automated haggling bots already set terms in commoditised transactions; the constraint is discretionary concession authority and reading the counterparty in higher-value deals.

dwa_title: Negotiate contracts for environmental remediation, green energy, or renewable resources.
rationale: These deals bundle regulatory liability, long-horizon environmental risk and multi-party public stakeholders, so terms must be judged and signed by an accountable professional rather than generated.

dwa_title: Resolve employee or contractor problems.
rationale: Employment grievances and contractor disputes require a trusted, legally accountable human to hear the parties and own the settlement; LLMs can only prep policy analysis and draft language.

dwa_title: Resolve operational performance problems.
rationale: Diagnosis of performance shortfalls is highly analysable from data, but implementing fixes usually requires directing people and physical processes, and someone must answer for the operational outcome.

dwa_title: Perform music for the public.
rationale: Live performance is valued precisely for the embodied presence of the performer before an audience; generated audio substitutes for recordings, not for the public act itself.

dwa_title: Respond to customer problems or complaints.
rationale: Chatbots and automated resolution flows already close a large share of routine complaints; escalation, emotional de-escalation and goodwill concessions still pull in humans.

dwa_title: Answer customer questions about goods or services.
rationale: Product and service Q&A is retrieval over a known knowledge base, which deployed LLM assistants handle end-to-end; the main constraint is liability for wrong answers in regulated categories.

dwa_title: Correspond with customers to answer questions or resolve complaints.
rationale: Asynchronous written correspondence is the single most LLM-native customer task and is already automated at scale in email and ticketing systems.

dwa_title: Confer with other personnel to resolve design or operational problems.
rationale: The technical reasoning is well within model reach, but the activity is definitionally a negotiated exchange among colleagues who must converge on and own a design decision.

dwa_title: Collaborate with others to resolve information technology issues.
rationale: IT troubleshooting is heavily text- and log-based and increasingly agent-assisted, yet cross-team coordination and system access approvals keep humans in the loop.

dwa_title: Communicate with management or other staff to resolve problems.
rationale: The substance is organisational dialogue and alignment with managers; tools can summarise and draft but cannot be the party to an internal negotiation.

dwa_title: Collaborate with technical specialists to resolve design or development problems.
rationale: Models can supply and critique deep technical options, but the collaborative resolution with named specialists who sign off on the engineering choice remains human.

dwa_title: Communicate with government agencies.
rationale: Regulatory correspondence is document-centric and highly draftable, but filings and representations to agencies typically require an authorised, legally liable signatory.

dwa_title: Communicate technical information to suppliers, contractors, or regulatory agencies.
rationale: Translating and transmitting technical specifications is near-pure information work for a model, yet accuracy of what is certified to regulators or suppliers carries liability requiring a named human attestor.

dwa_title: Collaborate with outside groups to develop programs or projects.
rationale: Joint program development with outside organizations rests on trust-building, negotiation and shared commitment between institutions; AI can draft proposals and synthesize inputs but cannot hold the relationship or bind the parties.

dwa_title: Coordinate with external parties to exchange information.
rationale: Routine information exchange is largely message composition and routing, already partly handled by EDI/portals and well suited to LLMs, but deciding what may be disclosed to whom still needs a responsible human.

dwa_title: Collaborate with law enforcement or security agencies to share information.
rationale: Sharing information with police or security agencies carries legal privacy, evidentiary and safety liability that requires a named accountable person, even though the drafting and matching work is automatable.

dwa_title: Coordinate operational activities with external stakeholders.
rationale: Scheduling and status synchronization across organizations is increasingly systemized, but resolving conflicting priorities between independent parties requires someone with authority to commit resources.

dwa_title: Coordinate activities with suppliers, contractors, clients, or other departments.
rationale: Supply-chain and interdepartmental coordination has substantial automated tooling for the transactional layer; the binding constraint is negotiating exceptions and holding counterparties to commitments.

dwa_title: Represent the organization in external relations.
rationale: Representation is inherently a matter of a person standing for the organization and being answerable for what is said; delegation to a machine defeats the purpose of the role.

dwa_title: Coordinate artistic activities.
rationale: Marshalling performers, rehearsals and creative logistics requires on-site presence and real-time interpersonal direction; only the calendaring and logistics paperwork slices off.

dwa_title: Prepare staff schedules or work assignments.
rationale: Workforce-management software already generates compliant rosters from demand forecasts, skills and availability; human input mainly handles fairness complaints and last-minute exceptions.

dwa_title: Prepare activity or work schedules.
rationale: Activity and work scheduling is a constrained optimization problem that deployed planning and project software solves routinely.

dwa_title: Assign duties or work schedules to employees.
rationale: The optimization is solved by software, but actually assigning duties is an exercise of supervisory authority over named employees, with labor-relations consequences a system cannot own.

dwa_title: Coordinate safety or regulatory compliance activities.
rationale: Compliance and safety regimes typically designate a responsible officer by statute; automated monitoring and tracking assist, but liability for lapses cannot be transferred to software.

dwa_title: Manage documentation to ensure organization or accuracy.
rationale: Document classification, version control and completeness checking are well served by content-management systems plus LLM extraction; residual human role is attesting to accuracy in regulated records.

dwa_title: Visit individuals in their homes to provide support or information.
rationale: The defining feature is bodily presence in someone's home combined with a trust relationship; only the information-preparation sliver is machine-assistable.

dwa_title: Interact with patients to build rapport or provide emotional support.
rationale: Rapport and emotional comfort with a vulnerable patient is the deliverable itself, and in clinical settings it is expected to come from an accountable present human.

dwa_title: Support the professional development of others.
rationale: Models can generate development plans and feedback text, but mentoring depends on sustained relational credibility, sponsorship and organisational standing that software does not hold.

dwa_title: Encourage patients or clients to develop life skills.
rationale: Motivating behaviour change in clients hinges on a trusted human relationship and clinical accountability; digital coaching tools supplement rather than replace it.

dwa_title: Teach basic living or other adaptive skills to patients or caregivers.
rationale: Teaching dressing, feeding or transfer skills requires hands-on demonstration, physical guidance and safety oversight in the patient's real environment.

dwa_title: Teach life skills or strategies to clients or their families.
rationale: Content can be generated and even delivered conversationally, but tailoring to family dynamics and securing buy-in is relational work carried by a responsible practitioner.

dwa_title: Tutor students who need extra assistance.
rationale: AI tutors already deliver competent one-to-one explanation and practice; the binding constraint is sustaining motivation and diagnosing affective barriers in struggling learners.

dwa_title: Teach humanities courses at the college level.
rationale: Models handle humanities content and discussion prompts well, but accredited instruction, seminar facilitation and grading authority rest with a credentialed faculty member.

dwa_title: Teach physical science or mathematics courses at the college level.
rationale: Technical content is highly formalisable and well covered by models, yet lab supervision, live problem-solving and institutional certification keep an instructor in the loop.

dwa_title: Teach classes in area of specialization.
rationale: Preparation and explanation are strongly model-exposed, but classroom management and credentialed delivery remain human; specialisation may also demand hands-on demonstration.

dwa_title: Teach social science courses at the college level.
rationale: Content generation and assessment drafting are well within model reach; live discussion of contested social questions and grading responsibility anchor a faculty human.

dwa_title: Lead classes or community events.
rationale: Leading a live class or community event requires physical presence, group energy management and real-time crowd reading that no deployed system provides.

dwa_title: Guide class discussions.
rationale: The binding constraint is real-time multi-party facilitation: reading who is disengaged, managing conflict and drawing out reticent participants in a shared room, which no deployed system does, even though LLMs handle Socratic dialogue one-to-one well.

dwa_title: Instruct college students in social sciences or humanities disciplines.
rationale: The intellectual content of humanities and social science teaching is squarely in LLM territory, but accreditation and degree-granting require a named instructor of record who owns assessment and certifies student learning.

dwa_title: Instruct college students in physical or life sciences.
rationale: Laboratory supervision adds in-person safety responsibility on top of the accreditation requirement for a credentialed instructor, so only lecture content and feedback generation are offloadable.

dwa_title: Teach safety standards or environmental compliance methods.
rationale: Much compliance instruction is already delivered as standardised LMS modules, but regulators require a qualified trainer to attest to competency, and hands-on drills and equipment demonstrations still need a body present.

dwa_title: Train personnel to enhance job skills.
rationale: Content design, practice scenarios and feedback are highly LLM-exposed, but diagnosing an individual worker's skill gap and motivating them to change behaviour remains a relational act.

dwa_title: Train personnel in technical or scientific procedures.
rationale: Technical and scientific procedure training typically hinges on supervised hands-on demonstration and correction at the bench or machine, which caps what screen-delivered instruction can replace.

dwa_title: Conduct employee training programs.
rationale: Program authoring, scheduling and assessment are already largely software-mediated; the residual human work is live delivery, cohort engagement and adapting to organisational politics.

dwa_title: Train others on work processes.
rationale: Process knowledge is documentable and explainable by a model, but transfer usually happens through shoulder-to-shoulder demonstration on the actual workflow and tools.

dwa_title: Train personnel on proper operational procedures.
rationale: Operational procedure training usually ends in a competency sign-off on live equipment, and the verification step requires a qualified observer physically watching the trainee perform.

dwa_title: Train personnel.
rationale: Written at high generality, so the split depends on subject matter; the consistent constraint is that instruction-giving is cheap to automate while judging readiness and building trainee confidence is not.

dwa_title: Train sales personnel.
rationale: AI role-play and pitch-critique tools already cover much of the drilling, but sales coaching trades on credibility, motivation and modelling behaviour that a peer or manager supplies.

dwa_title: Instruct staff in work policies or procedures.
rationale: Policy and procedure content is fully codified text, so generation, delivery and comprehension checks are readily automated; what remains is answering edge-case questions and confirming that staff actually acknowledged and understood the rules.

dwa_title: Train staff members.
rationale: Content design, curricula and assessments are strongly LLM-exposed and e-learning platforms already carry much of the delivery, but reading learner confusion, motivating staff and certifying competence keeps a human trainer in the loop.

dwa_title: Instruct patients in the use of assistive equipment.
rationale: Fitting and coaching a patient on a walker, prosthesis or lift requires hands-on positioning and real-time safety correction at the bedside, and a licensed clinician is answerable if the patient falls or misuses the device.

dwa_title: Teach others to use computer equipment or hardware.
rationale: Explanatory content and troubleshooting dialogue are well within current models, but showing someone physically how to handle, connect or service hardware still benefits from co-presence.

dwa_title: Train others in computer interface or software use.
rationale: Software instruction is pure information transfer in the same medium the learner is already working in; interactive walkthroughs and conversational assistants already deliver it end-to-end for most users.

dwa_title: Teach others to use technology or equipment.
rationale: Heterogeneous category: the explanatory layer is highly automatable, but wherever the equipment is physical the trainer must be present to guide hands and verify safe operation.

dwa_title: Demonstrate activity techniques or equipment use.
rationale: Demonstration means performing the motion or operation bodily so a learner can imitate it; video can substitute for generic cases but not for adapting the demo to the individual in the room.

dwa_title: Teach exercise or fitness techniques.
rationale: App-based programming and computer-vision form feedback are commercially deployed, yet correcting technique to prevent injury and sustaining client motivation remain embodied and relational.

dwa_title: Teach medical procedures to healthcare personnel.
rationale: Procedural skill transfer requires supervised hands-on practice and a credentialed clinician who signs off on competence; patient-safety liability cannot be delegated to a system.

dwa_title: Train caregivers or other non-medical personnel.
rationale: Instructional content is easy to generate, but confirming that an anxious, often untrained caregiver can actually perform care tasks safely requires observation in situ and clinical responsibility.

dwa_title: Engage patients in exercises or activities.
rationale: Engaging a patient means physical guarding, hands-on assistance and moment-to-moment encouragement; the therapeutic relationship and fall-risk supervision are the substance of the task.

dwa_title: Train patients, family members, or caregivers in techniques for managing disabilities or illnesses.
rationale: Tailoring disease-management technique to a specific household while handling fear, grief and adherence is irreducibly relational, and a licensed professional must be accountable for the instruction given.

dwa_title: Conduct health or safety training programs.
rationale: Compliance e-learning already delivers much of this at scale, but regulators typically require a named competent person to certify the program and hands-on drills or equipment practice cannot be screen-based.

dwa_title: Train medical providers.
rationale: Curriculum design and didactic content are already largely machine-generatable and CME e-learning is deployed at scale, but competency sign-off, bedside/procedural coaching and accreditation responsibility bind the activity to a credentialed instructor.

dwa_title: Teach health management classes.
rationale: Standardised health-education content delivers well through digital programs, but behaviour change in a live class depends on reading group dynamics, motivating participants and tailoring advice to disclosed personal circumstances.

dwa_title: Supervise scientific or technical personnel.
rationale: Scheduling, review drafting and progress tracking are assistable, but directing and evaluating staff is an authority relationship in which a named manager must own personnel decisions.

dwa_title: Supervise medical support personnel.
rationale: Clinical delegation rules and licensure make a specific supervising professional legally answerable for what support staff do to patients.

dwa_title: Supervise workers providing client or patient services.
rationale: Overseeing service delivery requires on-the-spot observation of staff-client interaction and intervention authority that cannot be delegated to a system.

dwa_title: Supervise employees.
rationale: Algorithmic scheduling and performance analytics are widely deployed, but employment law and the relational substance of managing people require a responsible human supervisor.

dwa_title: Supervise patient care personnel.
rationale: Nursing and care supervision carries direct patient-safety liability and requires physical presence on the unit to assess acuity and reassign staff in real time.

dwa_title: Supervise technical medical personnel.
rationale: Regulatory frameworks for diagnostic and technical medical services name a qualified supervisor who must vouch for personnel competence and procedure quality.

dwa_title: Supervise laboratory work.
rationale: LIMS automation covers workflow tracking and QC flagging, but a designated laboratory director must certify protocol adherence, troubleshoot bench anomalies in person and sign off on results.

dwa_title: Supervise student research or internship work.
rationale: Models can critique drafts and suggest methods, but mentorship, research-integrity responsibility and institutional evaluation of the trainee rest with a named supervisor.

dwa_title: Supervise workers performing environmentally sustainable activities.
rationale: Compliance checklists and sensor-based monitoring can be automated, but directing crews in the field and attesting to environmental practice requires a present, accountable supervisor.

dwa_title: Supervise engineering or other technical personnel.
rationale: Technical review can be heavily assisted, but professional engineering responsibility and the authority to direct and appraise staff must attach to an identifiable licensed manager.

dwa_title: Supervise trainees.
rationale: The binding constraint is the developmental relationship: assessing a novice's readiness, correcting them in the moment and vouching for their competence requires a named human mentor, even though AI can draft curricula and feedback.

dwa_title: Supervise production or support personnel.
rationale: Scheduling and output tracking are already software-driven, but on-floor presence, discipline, safety responsibility and employment decisions require an accountable supervisor.

dwa_title: Direct activities of subordinates.
rationale: Algorithmic task dispatch exists and is widely deployed, but directing people carries legal employer authority and motivational weight that cannot be delegated to a system.

dwa_title: Supervise information technology personnel.
rationale: Ticket routing, workload dashboards and code review tooling automate the monitoring layer, but personnel evaluation, prioritisation conflicts and accountability for system outages rest with a human manager.

dwa_title: Serve on institutional or departmental committees.
rationale: Committee service is constituted by representation and deliberation among named members; an AI can prepare briefs and minutes but cannot hold a seat or a vote.

dwa_title: Coordinate forestry or agricultural activities.
rationale: Weather, biology and equipment variability force on-site judgment and crew coordination; farm-management software optimises scheduling but cannot own the field decisions.

dwa_title: Manage agricultural or forestry operations.
rationale: Managing a biological production system spans labour, capital, regulatory compliance and irreversible seasonal bets, so decision support helps but a responsible operator remains the constraint.

dwa_title: Direct surveying activities.
rationale: Survey data capture is heavily instrumented, but a licensed surveyor must direct field crews and certify boundary results with legal liability attached.

dwa_title: Direct design or development activities.
rationale: Models can generate and critique design options, but setting direction amid conflicting requirements and holding a team to it is a trust-and-authority function.

dwa_title: Coordinate cross-disciplinary research programs.
rationale: Synthesising across disciplines is where LLMs are strongest, yet the work is mainly brokering between specialists, funders and institutions, which requires standing and relationships.

dwa_title: Direct technical activities or operations.
rationale: Operational direction is increasingly instrumented by control and workflow systems, but technical authority over live operations carries safety and regulatory responsibility that names a person.

dwa_title: Coordinate software or hardware installation.
rationale: Software deployment orchestration is genuinely automated in mature environments, but hardware placement, vendor and user scheduling, and rollback decisions during failed installs still need a coordinator.

dwa_title: Direct scientific activities.
rationale: Setting research direction and leading scientific staff turns on contested priority judgments and personal authority over a team; AI can draft plans and synthesize literature but cannot own the direction.

dwa_title: Direct natural resources management or conservation programs.
rationale: Conservation program leadership involves stakeholder negotiation, regulatory accountability and field oversight; models help with monitoring data and plan drafting only.

dwa_title: Manage information technology projects or system activities.
rationale: Much IT project management is documentation, scheduling and status synthesis that tools and LLMs handle well, but tradeoff decisions and team coordination still require an accountable manager.

dwa_title: Manage scientific or technical project resources.
rationale: Resource allocation and tracking are highly structured optimization and reporting tasks, yet commitments to staff, sponsors and grantors must be authorized by a named person.

dwa_title: Direct medical science or healthcare programs.
rationale: Clinical and research program leadership carries licensure, regulatory and patient-safety liability that must attach to an identifiable clinician-administrator.

dwa_title: Coordinate training activities.
rationale: Scheduling, curriculum assembly and enrollment tracking are largely handled by LMS automation, but arranging instructors and reading learner needs keeps a coordinator in the loop.

dwa_title: Manage human resources activities.
rationale: Employment decisions carry legal exposure and the substance is handling people—grievances, discipline, hiring—so a responsible human must remain in place even where systems draft and screen.

dwa_title: Direct quality control activities.
rationale: Automated inspection and SPC systems catch defects, but sign-off on releases, corrective actions and regulatory conformity is a named quality manager's duty.

dwa_title: Prepare project budgets.
rationale: Cost estimating is structured numeric modeling well suited to models and templates; the binding constraint is that assumptions must be owned and defended by an accountable budget holder.

dwa_title: Direct financial operations.
rationale: Financial control carries fiduciary and statutory certification duties (e.g., officer attestation), so directing operations cannot be delegated to a system despite heavy analytic automation.

dwa_title: Direct fundraising or financing activities.
rationale: Securing donors or capital is fundamentally a trust-based relational sale; AI drafts prospect research and appeals but the ask depends on a person.

dwa_title: Prepare operational budgets.
rationale: Rolling forecasts and variance-driven budget builds are already semi-automated in FP&A software; the allocation choices and their defense before leadership remain a human responsibility.

dwa_title: Manage organizational or project budgets.
rationale: Forecasting, variance analysis and reallocation modelling are highly tractable for software, but trade-off decisions among competing claimants and fiduciary sign-off require a named budget owner.

dwa_title: Manage financial activities of the organization.
rationale: Organization-wide financial stewardship carries statutory certification and fiduciary liability (e.g. officer attestation), so a human officer must own it even when analysis is machine-generated.

dwa_title: Manage budgets for appropriate resource allocation.
rationale: Optimization tools can propose allocations from structured data, but the binding constraint is political negotiation among units and accountability for the resulting cuts.

dwa_title: Direct natural resources extraction projects.
rationale: Extraction site direction combines on-site supervision of crews and hazardous equipment with licensed safety and environmental responsibility that regulators pin to a named person.

dwa_title: Direct construction activities.
rationale: Directing construction means live field judgment over crews, subcontractors and unforeseen site conditions, with code and safety liability attaching to the responsible supervisor.

dwa_title: Direct installation activities.
rationale: Supervising installation crews requires presence at the work face to see conditions and redirect workers; only sequencing and documentation are offloadable.

dwa_title: Coordinate construction or installation activities.
rationale: Scheduling and clash-detection software handles much of the coordination logic, but reconciling trades and resolving on-site conflicts remains a negotiation among people.

dwa_title: Manage construction activities.
rationale: Project management tooling automates cost/schedule tracking, but contractual and safety accountability for the build rests with a licensed or designated manager on site.

dwa_title: Direct green energy production operations.
rationale: Generation plants run under heavy SCADA automation, yet directing the operation entails grid-compliance and safety responsibility plus physical intervention during abnormal events.

dwa_title: Manage operations, research, or logistics projects.
rationale: Planning, tracking and optimization of projects are strongly model-assisted, but ownership of stakeholder commitments and reprioritization under disruption stays with a manager.

dwa_title: Direct environmental development activities.
rationale: Environmental program direction turns on contested evidence, regulatory sign-off and stakeholder negotiation; analysis and reporting are the only cleanly automatable slices.

dwa_title: Direct healthcare delivery programs.
rationale: Clinical program direction is legally tied to licensed accountability for patient safety and to leading clinical staff, regardless of how much analytics is automated.

dwa_title: Direct industrial production activities.
rationale: Production scheduling and line analytics are software-assisted, but directing a plant means on-floor supervision of crews and safety-critical decisions that a named supervisor must own.

dwa_title: Direct energy production or management activities.
rationale: SCADA and automated dispatch already handle much of the control loop, but licensed operators must remain answerable for grid/plant decisions with catastrophic failure modes.

dwa_title: Direct facility maintenance or repair activities.
rationale: CMMS platforms automate work-order generation and prioritisation, but assigning, inspecting and signing off on physical repairs requires presence and a responsible supervisor.

dwa_title: Arrange delivery of goods or services.
rationale: Logistics and dispatch platforms already book, route and confirm deliveries end-to-end; only exception handling and negotiation with counterparties still pulls in a human.

dwa_title: Coordinate project activities with other personnel or departments.
rationale: Scheduling, status synthesis and cross-team messaging are highly model-exposed, but securing commitment across departments is fundamentally a negotiation between accountable people.

dwa_title: Direct department activities.
rationale: Departmental direction bundles staffing, discipline and resource allocation over identified employees — decisions an organisation must attribute to a responsible manager.

dwa_title: Coordinate reporting or editing activities.
rationale: Drafting, assignment triage and copy review are squarely in model capability, yet editorial accountability for what is published and the handling of writers stays with a named editor.

dwa_title: Manage preparation of special meals or diets.
rationale: Therapeutic menu planning against dietary restrictions is well-handled by software, but overseeing actual food preparation and allergen safety demands physical supervision and a clinically responsible person.

dwa_title: Coordinate resource procurement activities.
rationale: E-procurement systems already automate requisition, sourcing and reordering; supplier negotiation and contract commitment remain human-signed.

dwa_title: Coordinate operational activities.
rationale: Broadly stated coordination is largely information routing and scheduling that tools do well, but the binding constraint is getting people to act, which requires a person with standing.

dwa_title: Manage healthcare operations.
rationale: Healthcare operations sit inside licensure, accreditation and patient-safety regimes that require a named administrator or clinical leader to answer for decisions.

dwa_title: Direct organizational operations, projects, or services.
rationale: General organisational direction is the exercise of delegated authority over resources and people; capability aside, fiduciary and governance norms require an identifiable human principal.

dwa_title: Direct equipment maintenance or repair activities.
rationale: Scheduling and prioritising maintenance is software-assisted, but directing crews on physical equipment requires on-site supervision and a person answerable for safety lockouts and repair adequacy.

dwa_title: Coordinate sales campaigns.
rationale: Campaign planning, copy and analytics are highly LLM-exposed, but marshalling a sales team and negotiating priorities across stakeholders remains a coordination role held by a person.

dwa_title: Coordinate enforcement of laws or regulations.
rationale: Enforcement discretion and the deployment of officers carry statutory authority and due-process liability that must rest with a named official.

dwa_title: Provide health and wellness advice to patients, program participants, or caregivers.
rationale: Generic wellness guidance is already delivered by apps and chatbots, but individualised advice tied to a patient's condition triggers clinical accountability and depends on motivational rapport.

dwa_title: Advise patients on preventive care techniques.
rationale: Preventive-care content is protocolised and well within model capability; the constraint is licensure for patient-facing counselling and the behaviour-change relationship that drives adherence.

dwa_title: Advise patients on effects of health conditions or treatments.
rationale: Explaining prognosis and treatment effects is informed-consent territory: the content is textual but a licensed clinician must own the communication and its interpretation.

dwa_title: Advise patients on healthcare system processes.
rationale: Navigating referrals, coverage and paperwork is rule-based information retrieval that chatbots and payer portals already handle, though confused or distressed patients still need a human fallback.

dwa_title: Recommend types of assistive devices.
rationale: Device matching requires physical assessment and fitting of the individual body, and prescription-grade recommendations sit with a licensed therapist or clinician.

dwa_title: Advise customers on technical or procedural issues.
rationale: Technical support diagnosis over text and voice is already widely automated with retrieval over documentation; escalation of novel or irate cases is the residual human slice.

dwa_title: Advise customers on the use of products or services.
rationale: Product usage guidance is documented knowledge delivered conversationally, the canonical deployed use case for LLM assistants.

dwa_title: Recommend products or services to customers.
rationale: Recommender systems plus conversational agents already drive most retail suggestion at scale; only high-consideration or high-trust sales still hinge on a human relationship.

dwa_title: Advise others about environmental management or conservation.
rationale: Synthesising regulations, site data and best practice is strongly LLM-exposed, but conservation advice rests on contested trade-offs and often on certified sign-off tied to site inspection.

dwa_title: Advise others regarding green practices or environmental concerns.
rationale: The knowledge base on green practices is well-documented text that models handle well, but the binding constraint is that advice must be tailored to a client's specific operations and accepted by them, which requires contextual fact-gathering and persuasion.

dwa_title: Advise others on green energy or related technologies.
rationale: Technology comparison, incentive rules and sizing calculations are highly tractable for models; the constraint is site-specific data capture and the fact that a named engineer or consultant typically stands behind a recommendation involving capital expenditure.

dwa_title: Advise others about land management or conservation.
rationale: Land and conservation advice rests on site inspection, local ecological conditions and contested trade-offs between production and preservation, so remote text reasoning can only prepare and support the recommendation.

dwa_title: Provide technical guidance to other personnel.
rationale: Explaining technical matter is squarely in a language model's strength, but guiding personnel means diagnosing what the colleague actually misunderstands and staying answerable for the outcome of their work.

dwa_title: Provide technical support for software maintenance or use.
rationale: Deployed AI support agents already resolve a substantial share of software help requests end-to-end from documentation and logs; escalation for novel defects and irate users is the residual human slice.

dwa_title: Provide recommendations to others about computer hardware.
rationale: Matching specifications and budget to hardware options is a structured comparison task already performed by configurators and recommendation systems; mistakes are cheap and reversible.

dwa_title: Advise others on the development or use of new technologies.
rationale: Advising on emerging technology means forecasting under genuine uncertainty and convincing decision-makers to commit resources, so the model supplies synthesis while a human owns the bet.

dwa_title: Provide technical support for computer network issues.
rationale: Automated monitoring and scripted remediation cover routine faults, but the binding constraint is that many network problems terminate in cabling, hardware or on-site device access.

dwa_title: Recommend changes to improve computer or information systems.
rationale: Analysing system performance and drafting improvement proposals is strongly model-exposed; what blocks full automation is access to organisational constraints and the need for someone accountable when a recommended change breaks production.

dwa_title: Advise others on business or operational matters.
